method: 28 subagents: 23 page surfaces + 4 cross-cutting + synthesis; th-design design-bar + information-design lenses

audits.current_state: The home page is an "editorial archetype" triage cockpit: a left narrative column (mono date eyebrow + briefing-source pill, 44px two-line briefing headline, serif elaboration paragraph, rule-separated "Needs attention" list, 4-cell KPI strip) and a right index column ("Operations" butler list with runtime state/cost/sessions, and a "Now" signal list for approvals/QA/notifications/recent timeline). Below the grid sits a legacy cost band (shadcn Card "Cost Today" widget + "Most Expensive Sessions" table). All data comes from nine independently polled TanStack Query hooks (30s–5m intervals) merged client-side by deriveOverviewTriageModel in /home/tze/gt/butlers/frontend/src/components/overview/model.ts, which also derives per-source degraded states for four of the six signal sources.
audits.jarvis_gap: The top half is genuinely close in tone — a system that greets you, speaks in sentences, and lists exactly what needs you is the right idea, and the degraded-state discipline in model.ts is above average. But it is a JARVIS that can only point, never act, and sometimes points vaguely or lies: nothing on the page is actionable in place (no approve, no dismiss-issue, no re-run — every signal is a ferry to another page, and often to a generic page rather than the evidence), the fleet index is inert, everything is 30-second polling rather than a live pulse, there is no keyboard surface at all, and two honesty holes (fabricated spend sparkline, all-clear on a dead issues source) undercut the calm-confidence contract that is the page's entire reason to exist. A JARVIS-grade console would let the owner clear their whole queue — approve, dismiss, drill, trigger — from this one screen in under a minute, hands on keyboard, with every number provably live.
audits.redesign_concept: Keep the editorial voice, make it a command surface. The page stays a two-column briefing — the system speaking, then a quiet index — but every sentence and signal becomes a first-class object: deduplicated into a single signal registry (each fact appears exactly once, at the register its urgency earns), deep-linked to its root evidence, keyboard-navigable, and carrying its first action inline (Approve, Dismiss, Retry, Open session) so the owner can process the morning's queue without leaving the pane. Data arrives as a live stream, the KPI strip carries the numbers the owner actually checks daily (healthy/total, active sessions, cost today with a real trend, approvals), and every source that fails says so in its own row — the page is structurally incapable of showing calm it cannot prove.
redesign_moves: Collapse AttentionList + OperationsNowList + the KPI approvals cell into one deduplicated signal registry: owner-action signals (approvals, QA findings, notification failures, high issues) render once in Needs attention with an inline first action (Approve / Dismiss / Retry) executable from the row; the right column becomes a pure live-activity feed (running sessions with elapsed time, last events).

Make every row a full-width, focusable deep link to root evidence: stale/offline butler → /butlers/{name}, activity → the specific event/session, approval → the specific approval; kill all generic /system and /timeline hrefs and make ButlerIndex rows navigate to butler detail.

Add a keyboard loop: j/k roving focus across all rows, Enter to drill, a to approve, d to dismiss, r to refresh the briefing; register the page's live signals into the global command palette so 'approve pending' is reachable from anywhere.

Fold cost into the editorial register: replace the Card-chrome cost band with a 'Cost · today' KPI cell plus a real 7-day stripe (SessionStripeChart already exists) and a rule-separated top-sessions Section; delete the fabricated sparkline the same day.

Replace 30s polling with an SSE/WebSocket pulse for heartbeats, timeline, and approvals so 'active' means active now; give each butler row a live activity stripe (last 24h sessions) so the fleet's rhythm is readable at a squint.

Make degraded-state coverage total and symmetric: every one of the six sources (including issues and approvals) gets an explicit 'source unavailable' row and a briefing pill 'unavailable' state; the all-clear Voice line renders only when all sources verifiably loaded.

Let the briefing act, not just narrate: headline and elaboration sentences that reference a butler, an approval, or an incident become inline links into the same signal registry, so the system's prose is the fastest drill-down path of all.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/costs/CostWidget.tsx:52-62
findings.issue: The "7-day trend" sparkline is fabricated: bars are a hardcoded pseudo-random formula (`20 + ((i * 37 + 13) % 80)`) with a comment admitting it is a placeholder, yet it renders as real data with a data label. This actively misleads the owner about spend trend — the single worst sin on a trust-the-system dashboard (design-bar bias 1; design-language.md "the pill is always honest about what is rendering" applies doubly to charts).
findings.fix: Delete the fake bars immediately; render the real 7-day series from the spend API (a SessionStripeChart-style stripe already exists in components/dashboard/), or render nothing plus a "trend unavailable" note until the data is wired.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:83 and model.ts OverviewDerivationInput (no issuesError field)
findings.issue: issuesQuery.isError is never threaded into the model — on an issues-API failure the input falls back to [] and AttentionList renders the serene serif "Nothing waiting." The primary triage surface can show calm-all-clear while its main evidence source is down, exactly the failure mode ButlerIndex's own docstring warns against ("an empty list over a dead source must not read as a healthy, quiet system").
findings.fix: Add issuesError to OverviewDerivationInput; when set, render an explicit "Issues source unavailable" degraded row (role=alert) in the attention list and never the all-clear empty state. Same for approvalMetrics, which is also silently dropped from attention/now rows on error.

The fleet roster, the most natural drill-down on the whole pane (butler detail pages exist at /butlers/:name), is a dead end; a stale or offline butler shown here cannot be clicked to investigate. Violates the purpose doc's Detect→Diagnose loop and design-bar bias 1 (hunting).
findings.fix: Make each row a full-row Link to /butlers/{name}; add visible focus and hover states consistent with NowRow's link treatment.

findings.evidence: model.ts:164-171 (attentionRows) vs model.ts:438-494 (nowRows) vs RuntimeSummaryKpi.tsx:39-41

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/overview/AttentionList.tsx:128-141; hrefs from model.ts:369 (runtime → "/system") and model.ts:513 (activity → "/timeline")

Violates "instant drill-down from any signal to root evidence" and design-bar bias 1.
findings.fix: Make the entire attention row the link target (keep the arrow as a visual cue); deep-link every row — runtime rows to the affected butler's detail, activity rows to the event (e.g. /timeline?event=ID or the session view), approvals to the specific approval.

findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:171-190 + CostWidget.tsx/TopSessionsTable.tsx (shadcn Card, CardTitle "Cost Today", Badge)
findings.issue: The cost band is a different design language bolted under the editorial page: card chrome, title-case headers, secondary badges — on the one page design-language.md governs most explicitly ("rule-separated rows, no card chrome", "The KPI strip replaces card chrome"). Also DashboardPage.tsx:181 puts CostWidget in a lg:grid-cols-2 grid with a single child, leaving a permanently empty half-width cell.

findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx (no key handlers, no palette registration); docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md "Keyboard-first navigation and quick search for operational speed" (In Scope)
findings.issue: The most important screen has zero keyboard affordances: no row-to-row navigation, no Enter-to-drill, no shortcut to refresh the briefing or jump to approvals; ButlerIndex rows are not even focusable. The stated scope promises keyboard-first speed; the single pane doesn't deliver it (design-bar bias 7).
findings.fix: Add j/k (or arrow) roving focus across attention/now/butler rows with Enter to drill and a/d quick actions where applicable; register "go to approvals/issues/butler X" entries in the global command palette from this page's signals.

findings.evidence: BriefingStatus.tsx:47-53 pillContent; DashboardPage.tsx:108-112 fallbacks
findings.issue: A failed briefing request is indistinguishable from a deliberate template: source undefined renders the dim "templated" pill, and the headline shows "Good morning. / Checking in." regardless of error — and regardless of the actual time of day. The pill doctrine says it "names what it is showing"; an error masquerading as templated breaks that.

findings.evidence: CostWidget.tsx:13-16 formatCurrency vs ButlerIndex.tsx:149-151 formatCost

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/dashboard/RecentMoments.tsx and frontend/src/components/overview/NextList.tsx (no non-test importers)
findings.issue: Orphaned components sit in the dashboard/overview directories (RecentMoments, NextList) with tests but no page usage, misrepresenting the surface's composition to future maintainers.

audits.current_state: /butlers is a status-board rewrite (bu-hb7dh): a 4-column grid of butler tiles, each with an eligibility-colored left rail, name + activity chip, role tagline, a KPI quartet (SESS 24H / SPEND / LOAD / LAST), and a 24-hour activity stripe. A BoardHeader carries an eyebrow, "The staff, at a glance" title, a healthy/total pill, and a live clock; a BoardFooter aggregates fleet KPIs (active/offline/quarantined, sessions, spend, avg load). Data comes from useButlerStatusBoard, which joins six sources (butlers list, registry, heartbeats, spend, per-butler runtime-config and hourly-activity fan-outs) with partial-failure tolerance; quarantined/stale butlers get a click-to-restore chip wired to useSetEligibility. Loading/error/empty/stale-cache states are all handled via the Page status-board archetype.
audits.jarvis_gap: This page is a competent census, not an operator's console. It answers "is everyone alive?" honestly (rails, chips, degraded-pill logic show real care), but it stops at status: a quarantined butler shows no reason, an amber pill shows no cause, footer zeros can be fiction, and \"IDLE\" means the same thing for a butler that runs hourly and one that runs weekly — there is no notion of expected cadence, so the board cannot say \"chronicler is 3 days overdue\", which is the single most JARVIS-relevant fact about a fleet of cron-driven daemons. There is no triage: nothing collects what needs the owner; problem cells sit wherever the traffic sort puts them. And the only action on the page (restore) is an unlabeled 9px chip with a keyboard bug. JARVIS-grade means the board leads with \"2 things need you, here's why, here's the fix button\" and everything else is one calm green line — this page makes the owner scan 12 tiles and infer that themselves.
audits.redesign_concept: Turn the roster from a census into a triage board. The first screenful leads with an exceptions strip — every butler that needs the owner, with root evidence inline (quarantine reason, last error, \"silent 3d, expected daily\") and one-keystroke verb-labeled actions (Restore with undo, Trigger run, Open sessions). Below it, a stable-ordered grid (roster order, staffers grouped last) of the same rich tiles, where health is judged against each butler's own schedule rather than a generic idle/running binary, unknown is always rendered as unknown (never zero, never green), and every signal — amber pill, dark stripe cell, red rail — is a door that opens onto its evidence. On a good day the strip is a single line: \"All 12 healthy · 47 sessions · $3.12 today\" — calm confidence earned, not asserted.
redesign_moves: Add a needs-you triage strip above the grid: quarantined/stale/offline/overdue butlers listed with root evidence inline (quarantine_reason + quarantined_at from the registry API, last error, silence-vs-schedule delta) and explicit undoable actions (Restore, Trigger, Open sessions); collapses to one calm summary line when the fleet is healthy.

Judge health against each butler's own cadence: join the scheduler's cron expectations so the board distinguishes "idle, next run in 40m" from "silent 3 days, expected daily" — replacing the flat IDLE verb with the fact that actually matters for an autonomous fleet.

Freeze the grid: fixed roster order with staffers grouped last (honoring the vision's butler/staffer distinction), needs-attention badging instead of reshuffling, and arrow-key navigation across cells with Enter to open — spatial memory plus keyboard-first speed.

Adopt one truthful degraded-data grammar page-wide: unknown never renders as 0 or green; footer aggregates say "unavailable" or "≥ $X (partial)" per the degraded-mode doctrine; the amber pill becomes a popover naming exactly which sources are degraded, with a link to the health surface.

Make every signal a door: stripe cells get hover tooltips (owner-local hour + count) and click through to the sessions view filtered to that butler and hour; SPEND clicks to the spend tab; OFFLINE clicks to last logs — no dead-end signals.

Collapse the 2N-query fan-out into a single GET /api/butlers/board payload (rows, aggregates, quarantine reasons, hourly buckets) so the board paints in one round trip with no per-cell skeleton stagger.
Fix the restore interaction outright: verb-labeled affordance separate from the status chip, undo via toast, and keydown containment so keyboard activation never restore-and-navigates.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-butler-status-board.ts:335-336 and frontend/src/components/butlers/BoardFooter.tsx:95-96
findings.issue: Footer aggregates fabricate confident zeros when sources fail: totalSpendToday = sum of (costToday ?? 0) and totalSessions24h = sum of hourlyTotal (0 while loading/errored). If the spend endpoint or the hourly-activity queries error, the footer authoritatively shows "$0.00" and "0" sessions. Spend and hourly-source errors also do not feed sourcesPartiallyDegraded (hook line 351), so the header pill can stay green while the numbers are fiction. This violates the repo's own degraded-mode doctrine (CLAUDE.md: never render zeros as if real; show a metrics-unavailable indicator) and directly undermines the calm-confidence bar — the owner reads "fleet spent nothing today" when the truth is "unknown".
findings.fix: Thread per-source error flags into the footer: render "unavailable" (or "≥ $X, partial") for SPEND TODAY / SESSIONS 24H when the underlying source errored or is loading, and include spend/hourly failures in sourcesPartiallyDegraded so the header pill goes amber.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butlers/StatusBoardCell.tsx:296 (div role="link" onKeyDown) vs. 185-187 (button onClick stopPropagation)
findings.issue: Keyboard Enter on the restore chip fires restore AND navigates away. The restore button's stopPropagation only covers the click event; the keydown event bubbles from the nested <button> to the wrapping div role="link", whose onKeyDown calls navigate() on Enter or Space. A keyboard user activating "QUARANTINED" restores the butler and is immediately yanked to the detail page, losing the success/failure toast context. Space on the role="link" div also lacks preventDefault, so it scrolls the page. Violates design-bar bias 4 (keyboard-operable by default) and repeat-safe.
findings.fix: In the div's onKeyDown, ignore events whose target is not the div itself (e.target !== e.currentTarget), and preventDefault on Space before navigating.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/api/types.ts:2207-2208 (quarantine_reason, quarantined_at exist) vs. frontend/src/hooks/use-butler-status-board.ts:218 (only eligibility_state consumed)
findings.issue: The owner is asked to restore a quarantined butler with zero evidence. The registry API already returns quarantine_reason and quarantined_at, but the hook drops both; the cell shows only the word QUARANTINED and a one-click restore. This is the sharpest violation of "instant drill-down from any signal to root evidence" — the single moment this page demands a decision, it withholds the fact needed to make it.
findings.fix: Surface quarantine_reason and quarantined_at in the cell (tooltip/inline line or a focus peek) and next to the restore affordance, so restore is an informed action.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butlers/StatusBoardCell.tsx:181-198 (restore chip)
findings.issue: Restore — a write that re-enables routing to a possibly-broken butler — is hidden in a 9px underlined status word. The microcopy states the category ("QUARANTINED", "STALE") not the action ("Restore"), violating the information-design copy rule; there is no confirm and no undo; and because the entire cell is a click target, a mis-click aimed at opening the detail page can silently un-quarantine a butler. Nothing on the page teaches that the chip is actionable.
findings.fix: Replace the chip-as-button with an explicit action affordance (e.g. a small "Restore" button or hover/focus action row) labeled with the verb, and make restore undoable via the toast ("finance restored — Undo").

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butlers/StatusBoardCell.tsx:197,206 (heartbeatUnavailable ? "—" : ...) and use-butler-status-board.ts:259 (heartbeatUnavailable includes isPending)
findings.issue: heartbeatUnavailable masks states that do not depend on the heartbeat source: offline comes from the butlers list and quarantined/stale from the registry, yet the chip renders "—" whenever heartbeat data is unavailable — hiding a genuinely-known OFFLINE or QUARANTINED verdict. Because isPending is folded in, every chip in the fleet shows "—" during the initial heartbeat load. The rail still shows red/amber, so rail and chip contradict each other.
findings.fix: Only degrade the running/idle distinction when heartbeat is unavailable; keep OFFLINE / QUARANTINED / STALE labels (their sources are independent), and show a skeleton rather than "—" while heartbeat is merely pending.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butlers/BoardHeader.tsx:50-55 (pillDotClass) and use-butler-status-board.ts:351
findings.issue: The amber degraded pill is a dead-end signal: when sourcesPartiallyDegraded flips it amber, nothing anywhere on the page says which source degraded (heartbeat fleet-wide? registry? per-butler schema_unreachable?) or links to evidence. The owner sees amber, cannot diagnose, and must go spelunking in other pages — the exact detect→diagnose loop the single-pane doctrine exists to close.
findings.fix: Make the pill expandable (popover or inline line) listing the degraded sources with counts (e.g. "heartbeat source down; 2 butlers schema-unreachable") and a link to the relevant system/health surface.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-butler-status-board.ts:313-316 (sort by sessions24h desc)
findings.issue: The grid reorders on every 30s poll because it sorts by a live counter — cells migrate while the owner watches, destroying spatial memory ("finance is always top-left") and moving click targets under the cursor. Worse, ordering is by traffic volume, not by need: an offline or quarantined butler can sit in the last row while a chatty healthy one holds the top-left slot. Attention ordering on a monitoring surface should follow urgency, then stability.
findings.fix: Use a stable order (fixed roster order, or needs-attention first then roster order; staffers grouped last per the vision's butler/staffer distinction) so positions never shuffle on poll.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butlers/BoardHeader.tsx:51 (total === 0 returns bg-green-500) with ButlersPage.tsx:83 rendering the header in loading/error states
findings.issue: During the loading skeleton and the full-page error state, the header renders with zeroed aggregates: a GREEN dot beside "0/0 reporting" and "0 butlers". A green all-clear next to an error card is a small lie.
findings.fix: Render a neutral/skeleton pill (muted dot, "—/—") when aggregates.isLoading or isError.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butlers/BoardFooter.tsx:104 ("Active" = running-now) vs. EligibilityState "active" (use-butler-status-board.ts:33); BoardHeader.tsx:114 ("reporting" = computed healthy)
findings.issue: Vocabulary drift: footer "ACTIVE" counts butlers with running sessions, while "active" elsewhere means registry-eligible; the header pill says "reporting" but its number is a health computation (total − offline − quarantined), not a reporting count. One name per concept is violated twice on one screen.
findings.fix: Rename the footer cell to "Running" and the pill to "N/M healthy".

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butlers/ActivityStripe.tsx:64-91 (peak hour only in aria-label, UTC) and StatusBoardCell.tsx:249-281 (no axis, no tooltips)
findings.issue: The 24h stripe has no time axis and no per-cell hover detail — the owner cannot map a dark cell to an hour or a count. The only hour information (peak) lives in the aria-label, and in UTC rather than owner-local time, contradicting the Time primitive's owner-timezone convention.
findings.fix: Add per-cell tooltips ("14:00–15:00 · 6 sessions", owner-local) and faint now/−12h/−24h tick labels under the stripe.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-butler-status-board.ts:177-198 (two useQueries fan-outs per butler)
findings.issue: The board issues ~2N+4 requests (runtime-config + hourly-activity per butler; ~28 requests/minute at 12 butlers), producing per-cell skeleton stagger on the SESS KPI and stripe and scaling poorly as the roster grows. Perceived latency is a design property.
findings.fix: Add a single GET /api/butlers/board endpoint returning rows + aggregates + quarantine reasons + hourly buckets in one round trip.

audits.current_state: A tabbed per-butler console at /butlers/:name with a two-vocabulary mode toggle: "resident" mode (default) shows Overview / Activity / Logs / Approvals / Spend / Config / Memory, while "operator" mode swaps in Sessions / Skills / Schedules / Trigger / MCP / State / CRM / Models / Manage — plus bespoke domain tabs (Finances, Trips, Contacts, Investigations, etc.) per butler. The header shows identity (ButlerMark, activity dot, port/uptime) with Force Run / Logs / Config / Prompt (chat) / Pause actions. The Overview is a disciplined mono-eyebrow panel grid (status, sessions 24h, spend today, awaiting count, 24h activity stripe, recent events, pending approvals, config facts) built on shared atoms (Panel/KpiCell/KV/ErrorLine) with real loading, error, and empty states throughout.
audits.jarvis_gap: The bones are genuinely good — a coherent mono panel-grid language, real loading/error/empty states everywhere, a chat Prompt on every butler, and Force Run that lands you in the spawned session. But this is a well-organized filing cabinet, not JARVIS. A JARVIS console would open with what the butler did for you and what it needs from you, in words; this opens with counters and a stripe, and every signal is a cul-de-sac (events you can't click, an approval count capped at 5, a stripe that renders 'nothing happened' when data is missing). The operator/resident split means the owner must know a mode vocabulary before the right controls even exist on screen, and there is not a single keyboard path on the whole surface. The gap is not missing data — nearly everything needed is already fetched — it is that the page never composes that data into judgment, never links signal to evidence, and never lets a fast owner move at typing speed.
audits.redesign_concept: One butler, one console, no modes: a briefing-first operator page. The top third is the butler speaking — a generated one-line digest ('Triaged 14 emails overnight, flagged 2; needs your approval on 1 payment; next run 14:00') with the awaiting-you queue inline and approvable in place. The middle is a unified activity ledger — sessions, approvals raised, memory writes, log errors interleaved on one timeline, every row expanding to its root evidence (session transcript, approval detail, log context) without leaving the page. The bottom rail is a single command bar: type to prompt the butler, hit Enter to run, with palette-registered verbs (run, pause, open schedule) and bracket-key tab cycling. Everything operational (skills, schedules, MCP, state, models, manage) folds into one 'System' section because it is checked monthly, not hourly.
redesign_moves: Kill the mode toggle: one tab set — Overview, Activity (sessions + logs + events interleaved), Approvals, Spend, Memory, domain tab, System (config/skills/schedules/mcp/state/models/manage as sub-sections). Delete the auto-promotion machinery and the CRM base tab.

Replace the Overview KPI grid's top row with a narrative digest: what ran, what changed, what needs you, what's next (next cron fire is already in schedules data but shown nowhere on this page) — counters demoted to a quiet stat strip beneath it.

Make every signal a door: activity rows open the session drawer in place, stripe bars filter the ledger to that hour, approval rows approve/reject inline (the API exists) with a deep link for detail — never a bare link to a global list.

Unify Force Run / Trigger / Prompt into one persistent command bar at the page bottom: type-to-prompt with a default 'run tick' on empty Enter, complexity as a modifier, response streaming into the ledger.

Keyboard-first pass: 1-9 or [ ] cycles tabs, 'r' runs, 'p' pauses (with confirm), 'a' jumps to approvals; register per-butler actions in the command palette so 'run finance' works from anywhere in the app.

Honest degraded states: distinguish 'no activity' from 'metrics unavailable' on the stripe, use meta.total for all counts, and surface the butler's next scheduled run and last error in the header instead of port/uptime.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ButlerDetailPage.tsx:158-179, 339-369; frontend/src/pages/butler-detail-tabs.ts:14-43
findings.issue: The operator/resident mode split hides half the console behind an undiscoverable toggle: DetailModeSwitch is a bare lowercase word ('resident') at the end of the tab rail that labels the CURRENT mode while acting as a switch to the other. Sessions is unreachable in resident mode; Activity/Logs/Spend/Approvals are unreachable in operator mode. This is one owner's single workflow split into two vocabularies — the deep-link auto-promotion machinery (ButlerDetailPage.tsx:251-271) exists purely to paper over the mode seam. Violates design-bar bias 1 (never makes the user hunt) and bias 7 (discoverable power).
findings.fix: Collapse to one mode. Merge Sessions into the resident vocabulary (it is the primary drill-down surface), group the low-frequency operator tabs (Skills/Schedules/Trigger/MCP/State/Models/Manage) under a single 'Configure' or 'System' section, and delete the mode toggle and its promotion logic entirely.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerOverviewTab.tsx:151,174,219-226
findings.issue: The 'awaiting' KPI is capped at the query page size: useApprovalActions({limit: 5}) then awaitingCount = pendingActions.length, so the tile reads '5' when 20 approvals are pending. The response's meta.total is available (ButlerApprovalsTab reads it at line ~140) but ignored here. On a console whose core promise is 'exactly what needs the owner', an undercounted attention queue misleads.
findings.fix: Use meta.total for the KPI value; keep the 5-row preview list in the 'awaiting your action' panel with a 'N more' link.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerOverviewTab.tsx:104-121, 228-261; frontend/src/router-config.tsx:87
findings.issue: Overview signals are dead ends: recent-activity rows (session_completed, memory_write) are plain text with no link to the session or memory record; the 24h activity stripe bars are not clickable to filtered sessions; approval rows link to the global /approvals list with no ?butler filter and no /approvals/:id route exists, so the owner must re-find the exact item they just clicked. Violates the bar's 'instant drill-down from any signal to root evidence'.

audits.current_state: /sessions is a cross-butler session log browser: a window-true KPI strip (total/success-rate/tokens/top-butler), a stacked per-butler stripe chart, a six-field filter bar mirrored to the URL, and a keyset-paginated 10-column table whose rows open a right-side drawer with metadata, prompt, tool-call list, result/error, tokens, cost JSON, and trace ID. /sessions/:id is a separate full-page rendering of the same record — reached only from OTHER surfaces (episodes, notifications, calendar, chat, ingestion, trigger tab), never from the sessions list itself — and shows a poorer subset of fields than the drawer. Solid bones (URL-as-state filters, honest window-true aggregates, accessible clickable rows) wrapped around drill-down dead ends and a split-brain detail experience.
audits.jarvis_gap: This surface is a competent log browser, but it is interrogation-shaped, not JARVIS-shaped: the owner must come with a question (filter, paginate, click) and the page answers only what was asked. Nothing is surfaced proactively — no pinned failures with error excerpts, no anomaly callouts (failure spike, cost spike, session running 10x longer than its median), no live view of what the fleet is doing right now. The evidence chain breaks at every joint: trace links drop their trace, the drawer can't reach the full page, the full page shows less than the drawer, and the tool-call 'timeline' has no time. Cost — the owner's actual money — is buried in a collapsed JSON blob. A JARVIS-grade console would open on 'here's what's running, here's what failed, here's what it cost' and let the owner fall through any of those into a complete, timestamped, causally-linked dossier in one keystroke; today that path requires manual filter surgery and hand-edited URLs.
audits.redesign_concept: Rebuild Sessions as the fleet's flight recorder: a single addressable dossier per session (one component, rendered as overlay on the list or full page, always URL-true) sitting under an anomaly-first ledger. The first screenful answers three questions without a click — what is running now (live, elapsed timers), what failed recently (pinned with one-line error excerpts), and what the window cost (dollars, window-true) — and every signal on the page is a real link into evidence: a tool-call Gantt with per-call latency and tokens, a causal chain strip (ingestion event → routing → this session → child sessions → outbound notifications) built on trace_id, and cross-links that carry their context instead of dropping it.
redesign_moves: Unify drawer and detail page into one URL-addressable SessionDossier: row click routes to /sessions/:id (butler resolved server-side) rendered as an overlay over the preserved filtered list — shareable, refresh-safe, Escape returns exactly where you were; delete the split-brain drawer/page pair.

Make trace_id the spine of drill-down: a causal-chain strip inside the dossier showing the originating ingestion event, sibling/child sessions, and outbound notifications on one line, each a working link; ingestion timeline gains a trace filter so the trace chip lands on correlated evidence.

Replace the tool-call list with a real execution timeline: per-call start/duration/tokens recorded at source and rendered as a mini-Gantt so a slow session visually confesses where its time went; kill the regex name-guessing.

Anomaly-first ledger: default lens pins running sessions (ticking elapsed timers) and recent failures (inline one-line error excerpt) above the chronological flow, with a live streaming transcript view for in-flight sessions — watch a butler work in real time.
Money as a first-class axis: $ per session in the table, window-true cost KPI, cost-by-butler in the stripe chart tooltip, and a structured (not JSON) cost breakdown in the dossier.

Keyboard loop for the triage habit: j/k row navigation, Enter opens dossier, f toggles failed-only, r toggles running-only, / focuses debounced filter input, and window presets (1h/24h/7d) replace raw date pickers.
One refresh authority: a single shared auto-refresh context governing table, KPI strip, and chart together, so the toggle means what it says.

audits.current_state: /timeline (nav: Telemetry → Timeline) renders a cross-butler event stream from GET /api/timeline, which fans out session rows from every butler DB plus notifications from the switchboard DB. The page is a filter card (butler chips + three event-type chips: Session/Notification/Error) above a card containing a dot-and-line list: absolute timestamp, butler badge, type badge, truncated one-line summary. Session/error rows link to /sessions/:id; notification rows expand inline to a raw JSON dump; consecutive "heartbeat"-looking events collapse into a group row. Pagination is a manual "Load more" cursor, with a 10s auto-refresh toggle in the header. Loading skeleton, empty state, and error-with-retry states exist and are tested (TimelinePage.test.tsx).
audits.jarvis_gap: Far. A JARVIS-grade fleet chronicle would answer "what has my staff been doing, and does anything need me?" the moment it opens — errors and failed deliveries triaged to the top, quiet periods compressed, a live tail that never goes stale, and one keystroke from any row to its root evidence. What exists is a flat, paginated log viewer whose trust properties are actually broken: the error filter under-reports, notifications can silently vanish, simultaneous events fall through the cursor, and real owner events get mislabeled as heartbeats by a substring match. Worse, the product already contains the JARVIS-grade version of this exact surface — the ingestion dispatch ledger shipped in the bu-4utdw redesign — making /timeline read as an abandoned predecessor rather than the fleet's system-of-record. It is the difference between a security-camera hard drive and a butler who briefs you.
audits.redesign_concept: Make /timeline the fleet chronicle: the single trustworthy record of everything the household staff did, rendered in the same dispatch-ledger language as the ingestion timeline. It opens pinned to now as a live tail — day and hour group headers, hairline-divided dense rows, an activity histogram scrubber with error overlay for jumping to any moment — with an attention strip above the stream that triages what actually needs the owner (failed sessions, undelivered notifications) and compresses heartbeat noise into honest one-line rollups. Every row peeks into a typed drawer (URL-backed) with a hard link to its root evidence (session transcript, notification record), every filter is URL-backed and saveable, every source is honest about degradation, and the whole thing drives from the keyboard.
redesign_moves: Unify the two Timelines: rebuild /timeline on the ingestion ledger system (hour-group headers, hairline rows, toolbar with range picker + search + saved views, URL-backed peek drawer) and add source facets — sessions, notifications, ingestion events, errors — so one chronicle replaces both the stale page and the vocabulary fork.

Lead with an attention strip, not filters: errors and failed notification deliveries in the active window pinned above the stream with counts and jump-to; the raw stream becomes supporting evidence below, restoring 'calm confidence at a glance'.

Replace auto-refresh-toggle + Load More with a real live tail: pinned-to-now streaming, an 'N new events' pill when scrolled into history, and a volume histogram scrubber (error overlay) to jump to any time — killing the stale-accumulator and invisible-failure bugs structurally.

Move event semantics server-side and make them honest: trigger_source-based heartbeat classification with correct rollup copy ('32 ticks · 8 butlers · 1 failed'), composite (timestamp,id) keyset cursor, event_type filtering in SQL, and a per-source degraded flag in the envelope rendered as a partial-data banner.

Typed peek drawer for every row: session rows show duration/cost/trigger/success with a transcript link, notification rows show channel/recipient/delivery status with a link to the Notifications record — no raw JSON dumps, no per-type interaction inconsistency.

Keyboard-first: j/k/enter list navigation, '/' focuses search, URL-backed filters registered as command-palette presets ('Timeline: errors today'), making the chronicle the fastest diagnostic entry point in the console.
Delete the dead ActivityFeed.tsx component and its duplicate heartbeat/relative-time logic as part of the migration.

findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/timeline.py:221-232, 264

Filtering to Error therefore shows only failures among the newest ~51 sessions and computes has_more=false, so the Load More button disappears — the owner concludes 'only these N errors exist' when older errors are silently unreachable. This breaks the hot diagnostic path (detect → diagnose) the single-pane doc promises.
findings.fix: Push event_type into the SQL predicate (WHERE success=false for errors) so pagination and has_more are computed over the filtered set, and add a test asserting deep error pagination.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/TimelinePage.tsx:43-57, 80-85

findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/timeline.py:267-269

audits.current_state: /notifications is a single-view delivery log for outbound messages the fleet sent the owner. It stacks four all-time stat cards (Total/Sent/Failed/Failure Rate) plus per-channel count badges, a filter bar (free-text butler, channel/status selects, day-granular since/until dates), and a 20-row offset-paginated table showing status badge, butler, recipient, channel, 60-char-truncated message, and relative time. audits.jarvis_gap: This surface is a competent delivery log but far from an operator console. A JARVIS-grade pane would answer three questions instantly: did my fleet reach me (windowed health, live), what failed and why (failures pinned, full error, retry chain as one story), and what exactly was said (full message on demand, one keystroke to the originating session or trace). Today the health signal is an all-time counter, failures are interleaved with routine rows, retry chains render as disconnected rows with a filter option that can never match, the message content is capped at 60 hover-only characters, and one of the two drill-down links is a dead end. The owner must click-acknowledge even successful messages — the page creates mental labor instead of absorbing it. audits.redesign_concept: Rebuild /notifications as the fleet's Outbound Delivery console: a triage strip of failures needing the owner (with retry, scoped acknowledge, and undo) pinned above a live chronological ledger of everything the fleet told the owner. Health is windowed and clickable — per-channel and per-butler delivery sparklines for the last 24h/7d that double as filters. Every row expands in place to the full message, metadata, error, and delivery chain (pending→failed→retried→sent grouped as one logical message), and every id is a working deep link: one keystroke to the originating session, one to the pre-filtered trace timeline. Sent messages are a passive record requiring nothing from the owner; only failures ever ask for action.
redesign_moves: Split the page into a pinned 'Needs attention' failure queue (retry + acknowledge with undo, scoped to visible filters) above a passive chronological ledger; delete read-tracking and the Mark read/Dismiss pair on sent rows entirely.

Replace the four all-time stat cards with a windowed delivery-health strip: sent/failed/failure-rate sparklines per channel and per butler over a 24h/7d toggle, each segment clickable to apply that filter — reusing the ingestion timeline's range vocabulary.

Group retry chains: collapse pending→failed→retried→sent rows sharing session+message into one logical message with a delivery-attempt timeline inside the expanded row, and fix the status filter to operate on effective status.

Make every row expandable (click/Enter) to full message body, metadata JSON, full error, and working deep links — including passing the trace id into /ingestion?q=<trace_id> instead of the current dead link.

Rebuild the filter bar as URL-backed state: butler becomes a roster select with counts, statuses become toggle chips showing live counts, dates become range presets; keep the table rendered via placeholderData during refetch so paging never flashes a skeleton.

Go live: poll or stream new notifications with a non-disruptive 'N new' pill, and surface a failed-delivery count badge on the nav item so the owner sees delivery trouble from anywhere in the dashboard.
Add keyboard-first operation: j/k row navigation, Enter to expand, e to acknowledge, r to retry, and command-palette entries for 'failed notifications last 24h'.

audits.current_state: /issues renders a single card listing grouped problems across the fleet: live "butler unreachable" probes plus all-time audit-log error groups (normalized by first-line error message), sorted by last-seen recency and polled every 30s. Each row shows a severity badge, butler name (or "N butlers"), a one-line description, occurrence count with first/last seen times, an optional "View" link, and a Dismiss button; a header toggle swaps to a dismissed-issues view with per-row Restore. Dismissals persist server-side (public.dismissed_issues) with optimistic cache updates. There are no filters, no search, no pagination, no keyboard path, and no detail expansion.
audits.jarvis_gap: Far. A JARVIS-grade console would be the fleet's triage inbox — the one place where 'something is wrong' becomes 'I understand it and fixed it' without leaving the screen. Today's page is a passive, unfiltered, all-time error list whose two core promises both fail: the evidence link silently drops its filters, and acknowledging an issue permanently mutes that failure signature forever. There is no global alerting (a dead butler raises no badge anywhere), no remediation (can't re-run the failed schedule, ping the butler, or open the failing session), no keyboard loop, and no visual kinship with the rest of the redesigned dashboard. It detects, but cannot diagnose or act — two of the three loops the single-pane doctrine exists to serve.
audits.redesign_concept: Turn /issues into the fleet's attention queue: a dense, severity-first ledger built on the system's Row/StateDot/ButlerMark vocabulary, where every row expands inline to its root evidence (the matching audit rows, the failing session trace, the affected butlers) and carries the remediation for its type — re-run the schedule, ping or restart the butler, open the session — so detect → diagnose → act completes on one screen. Acknowledgement is a triage state, not an oubliette: acked issues resurface automatically the moment they recur, flagged as recurrences, and every ack is a keyboard stroke with an undo toast. The queue's critical count lives on the sidebar so the page only needs visiting when something genuinely needs the owner — and when it does, silence everywhere else means health.
redesign_moves: Replace dismiss-forever with acknowledge-until-recurrence: persist dismissed_at, resurface any group whose last_seen_at exceeds it with a 'recurred after ack' marker, and add explicit snooze durations — the ack becomes a triage state instead of a permanent mute.

Make every issue expandable to root evidence inline: the group's recent audit rows, full error text, per-butler occurrence breakdown, and a direct link to the failing session/trace — and fix the deep-link contract (key/actor/since) so 'open in audit log' actually arrives filtered.

Attach remediation to issue types: unreachable → 'ping now' / open daemon status; scheduled_task_failure → 'run schedule now' / pause schedule; closing the act loop from the same row that raised the alarm.

Rebuild the list in the system's design language: Row-based ledger with StateDot severity (red/amber), ButlerMark chips per affected butler linking to /butlers/{name}, monospace error signatures, occurrence sparkline, and a status summary strip (N critical / N warning / last change) replacing the redundant card header.

Badge the fleet: a live critical-issue count on the Issues nav item (matching the QA/Approvals pattern) plus a shell-level strip for unreachable butlers, so the page pulls the owner in only when needed.

Add a triage toolbar and keyboard loop: Pill filters for severity/butler/time window with text search, default 7-day window over the all-time backlog, j/k row focus, e = acknowledge (with undo toast), o = open evidence, and command-palette entries for the hot actions.
Collapse the dismissed-view mode toggle into a filter state ('active / acked / all') so restoring a mis-acked issue is one Pill click, not a context switch.

findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/issues.py:195-204 with audit_grouping.py grouping key = normalized error message

This silently hides new critical failures — the opposite of 'calm confidence' (the owner believes silence means health).
findings.fix: Store dismissed_at and resurface any group whose last_seen_at > dismissed_at, flagged 'recurred after ack'; optionally offer explicit snooze durations. Rename the action from Dismiss to Acknowledge to match the semantics.

audits.current_state: A single-route page (AuditLogPage.tsx) that lists public.audit_log rows in a 4-column table (relative time, actor, action, target) with three free-text/date filters (actor, action, since), offset-based Previous/Next pagination at 20 rows/page, and a 30s auto-refetch. Rows click-expand to a detail panel showing actor/action/target/IP/request_id/note. It accepts ?key= and ?actor= deep-links (from the secrets passport and permissions pages) rendered as removable chips. It is read-only and shows no outcome, metadata, or links to any other surface.
audits.jarvis_gap: Far. A JARVIS-grade audit surface is the fleet's flight recorder: it opens on the privileged/mutation events that matter, makes failures jump out, and pivots from any entry to the session, credential, or butler that produced it in one keystroke. Today's page is a generic CRUD admin table: it opens on heartbeat/GET noise, hides the stored outcome and evidence columns entirely, dead-ends every identifier, breaks its own expand interaction (detail renders at the table bottom), and is mouse-only on a dashboard whose stated purpose is keyboard-first operations. The backend already has almost everything needed (privileged preset, metadata/result/error columns, target index, per-entry endpoint) — the frontend simply doesn't use it, so the gap is a presentation-layer failure, not a data one.
audits.redesign_concept: Recast /audit-log as the fleet's flight recorder — a dense, keyboard-driven forensic ledger where the default view is the privileged event stream (mutations, security actions, failures) with routine heartbeat/GET traffic collapsed into quiet summary bands. Outcome is the primary visual signal: failures surface red and float a persistent 'recent failures' facet. Filtering is faceted, not typed-from-memory — actor, action, outcome, and time-window chips built from the live vocabulary, all URL-addressable so any surface can deep-link both in and out. Every row expands in place to full evidence (exact timestamp, result, error, metadata JSON), and every identifier is a pivot: request_id opens the trace/session, actor opens the butler, target opens the credential passport or resource that was touched. New entries arrive as a non-disruptive 'N new events' pill; j/k/Enter drives the whole loop without a mouse.
redesign_moves: Default the feed to kind=privileged and collapse heartbeat/GET noise into single-line 'N routine events over 2h' bands that expand on demand — the first screenful becomes mutations and security events only.

Surface the stored-but-invisible evidence: extend the API to return result/error/metadata, add a per-row outcome dot, red treatment + one-click 'failures only' facet for errors, and a formatted metadata JSON viewer in the expanded panel.

Fix expansion into a true inline drawer rendered under the clicked row, keyboard-driven (j/k to move, Enter to expand, y to copy request_id), with exact second-precision timestamps in both column and panel.

Turn every identifier into a pivot: request_id → session/trace viewer, actor → butler detail, target schemes (u:google, butler:qa, rule:42) → passport/butler/rule pages — closing the loop with the passport and permissions pages that already link in.

Replace free-text exact-match inputs with faceted typeahead chips fed by a distinct actor/action endpoint, plus time-range presets (1h, 24h, 7d, custom) and an outcome facet; keep all filters in the URL as the single source of truth.
Move to cursor pagination with keepPreviousData and ~2x row density; deliver live updates as a 'N new events' pill at the top instead of a silent 30s refetch that shifts offset pages.
Add a compact top strip of aggregate signal — events/failures in the current window per actor — so the page answers 'is anything acting abnormally?' before the owner reads a single row.

The page never exposes or defaults to it, so the owner's first glance is operational noise, not the mutations/security events an audit surface exists to show. The action vocabulary (~100 writer call sites) is undiscoverable, so the owner must already know exact strings. Violates information-design (defaults/discoverability) and bias 8 (perceived speed).

audits.current_state: /approvals is a two-pane "dispatch dossier": a left rail of pending approvals and a right dossier (title, serif Why, evidence lines, proposed-action JSON, referenced entities resolved from UUIDs) with a floating Approve/Deny/Defer cluster, live WebSocket updates, optimistic decision flow with rollback, honest approved-vs-dispatched toasts, plus a bottom band holding a quiet-hours policy editor and a last-30 history list. /approvals/rules is a separate shadcn Card/Table CRUD page for standing auto-approval rules (filter, create via raw-JSON constraints, revoke via window.confirm). An autonomy-suggestions banner on /approvals proposes promoting frequent approvals into standing rules or revoking failing ones.
audits.jarvis_gap: The dossier core is genuinely close to the right shape — why/evidence/proposed-action as a briefing, optimistic decisions, honest dispatched-vs-queued toasts, UUID-to-name digest. But a JARVIS gate is a trust console, and this is a review inbox: the queue is arrival-ordered with no risk or expiry ranking; the hot loop has no keyboard path; deciding item A freezes item B's controls; there is no deep link from a "needs you" signal to the decision; evidence dead-ends with no route to the originating session or trace; decided items cannot be reopened for audit; a fetch failure impersonates an empty queue; and the entire standing-autonomy layer — the record of what the fleet may already do without asking — is an orphaned URL the owner cannot reach from the product. The owner can approve things here, but cannot see, tune, or verify the shape of the autonomy they have granted, which is the actual job of this surface.
audits.redesign_concept: One Trust Console: approvals, standing rules, and autonomy suggestions unified as a single ledger of "what the fleet may do, what it is asking to do, and what it did." The left rail is a risk-and-expiry-ranked queue triaged entirely from the keyboard; the center dossier is a briefing that links every claim to its source (session, trace, entity, contact) and every decision to its consequence (dispatched, stalled, retried); a persistent Autonomy panel shows, per butler and tool, the current trust level as a tunable spectrum — from "always ask" through scoped standing rules to full autonomy — with each grant carrying live usage counts and a one-keystroke revoke. Every approval is a URL, every decision teaches the system ("approve — and stop asking for this shape?"), and failure states are louder than success states, because this page is where trust is either earned or quietly corrupted.
redesign_moves: Merge /approvals/rules into /approvals as an always-visible Autonomy panel (per butler × tool trust spectrum with live use counts and inline revoke), deleting the orphaned CRUD page and the shadcn-admin idiom with it.

Make triage keyboard-native: j/k to walk the rail, a/d/x to approve/deny/defer, enter to expand evidence, ? for the cheat sheet — with per-item mutation state so a decision on one item never freezes the next.

Give every approval a URL (/approvals/:id) and wire notifications, history rows, and autonomy suggestions to deep-link into the dossier; decided dossiers render read-only with decided_by/decided_at provenance.

Rank the queue by consequence: expiry countdown chips, blast-radius weighting (outbound messages > data writes), butler grouping — so the first screenful is exactly what most needs the owner, not what arrived first.

Wire the dossier to root evidence: originating session/trace link in the header, evidence lines resolving to their source records, referenced entities and target contact linking to their pages — completing the Detect→Diagnose→Act loop on one screen.

Make decisions teach: after N similar approvals, the digest line itself offers 'approve — and always allow <scope>?' inline, replacing the detached blue/amber suggestion cards; confirming shows the created rule in the Autonomy panel immediately.

Invert failure visibility: a failed queue fetch, a stalled approved-but-unrun dispatch, and a dropped live stream each get explicit amber states with retry affordances; green is reserved for executed, and an empty queue is only shown when the fetch actually succeeded.

audits.current_state: A single 6,472-line workspace page (CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx) rendering a unified calendar over provider (Google) and butler-internal events: user/butler views; month/week/day/list ranges; drag create/move/resize with an undo ghost and recurrence scope sheets (this/following/series); a natural-language quick-add with parse-then-confirm; find-time with ranked slots drawn as grid ghosts; toggleable Activity (audit log), Proposals (butler-extracted events), and Duplicates panels; a Sources dialog with per-source sync health, primary-calendar control, and recovery sync; ICS export/import/subscribe; a search palette; and opt-in cross-domain overlays with a "tomorrow at a glance" briefing card and a meeting-prep rail in the detail panel. audits.jarvis_gap: This is the deepest, most honestly-engineered surface in the dashboard — real undo, recurrence scope sheets, soft-failure detection on every mutation, degraded-mode labeling, provenance links to sessions. audits.current_state: GroupsPage (/home/tze/gt/butlers/frontend/src/pages/GroupsPage.tsx) is a single paginated table of the relationship butler's contact groups — Name, Description, Members (count only), Created, Labels — over GET /api/relationship/groups. Groups themselves are read-only by spec (created via the butler's group_create/group_add_member tools). The page is deliberately absent from the sidebar (dashboard-shell spec) and is reachable only via Butler Detail → relationship → CRM tab → Quick Links, whose sibling "Contacts" link now redirects away to /entities — leaving Groups as the stranded last vestige of the retired contacts CRM surface.
audits.jarvis_gap: Very far. A JARVIS-grade view of "groups" would be social situational awareness: which circles are healthy, which are going cold, who inside them needs attention next — with one keystroke from any signal to the member and the evidence. What ships is a hidden, three-clicks-deep admin table that shows a count it won't let you open, lies ("No groups found") when the API fails, offers only label housekeeping as its interactivity, and is discoverable neither in the sidebar nor the command palette. It is the orphaned tail of a retired contacts CRM (its sibling /contacts route now redirects to /entities), and it delivers none of the relationship butler's Dunbar/cadence intelligence that the manifesto makes binding. The gap isn't polish — the page answers no operator question at all.
audits.redesign_concept: Retire the standalone /groups vestige and rebirth groups as "Circles" — a first-class lens on the relationship surface where contacts already live (the entities index / Plex). Each circle is a living unit of social attention, not a database row: a compact card or dense row showing member avatars, size against its Dunbar tier, last group interaction, cadence health (fresh / due / going cold), and upcoming member dates — sorted by attention-needed. One click expands into the member roster (each member deep-linking to their entity detail with interaction history), and labels become shared filter chips with a full lifecycle. The owner glances and knows which parts of their social world the butler is tending and which need them; everything else is one keystroke away via the palette.
redesign_moves: Kill the orphan: delete the standalone /groups page and mount groups as a 'Circles' lens inside /entities/index (where /contacts already redirects), registered in nav-config so both sidebar context and command palette can reach it — one relationship surface instead of a stranded vestige.

Make every circle open: expandable row / detail drawer backed by the already-built GET /groups/{id} members endpoint (client.ts getGroup is exported and unused today), with each member linking to /entities/:entityId — count becomes roster becomes person in two clicks.

Turn count into health: per-circle last-group-interaction (interaction_log_group data), overdue-cadence badge derived from Dunbar tier, and upcoming birthdays/anniversaries among members; default sort = most attention-needed, so the first screenful is the circles going cold.

Honest async states: wire useGroups error/refetch into the Page primitive's error+onRetry region; empty state names the real creation path ('ask the relationship butler to create groups') instead of implying an on-page action that doesn't exist.

Full label system in one place: swatch-based color picker with auto-contrast text (replace hardcoded #fff-on-any-hex), rename/recolor/delete with usage counts, inline label creation inside the assign dialog, and undo-toast on removal.

Drop pagination for a personal-scale list: single client-filtered view with type-ahead name search (keyboard-first), keepPreviousData for any remaining fetches — no skeleton flash, no Previous/Next chore for a dataset of a dozen circles.

Add an agency affordance: from a circle, one action to hand the butler work ('log a gathering with this circle', 'plan a reconnect') so the surface feeds the butler loop instead of terminating in read-only glass.

audits.current_state: The health suite is a new editorial /health landing (Voice briefing + 4-cell vitals KPI strip + insight-driven attention list, all real backend reads with LLM cost guards) plus six sub-pages reframed into the Dispatch rule-list language: measurements (trend rule-list + recharts chart + reading log), medications (adherence-stated rows with inline dose logging and a next-doses rail), conditions, symptoms (severity glyphs), meals (day-grouped with nutrition totals rail), and research (expandable notes). All six are genuine CRUD over the fact store with dialogs, filters, pagination, and 30s auto-refresh; the 2026-06-20 redesign brief's deterministic backend epic (trend, adherence, nutrition summary, insights reader, briefing) is visibly wired.
audits.jarvis_gap: The suite has JARVIS bones — a butler that speaks (Voice briefing with honesty pill), a scheduled insight engine feeding an attention list, and real deterministic reads under every number — but it behaves like a well-dressed filing cabinet, not an operator console. The single biggest gap is that the story and the evidence are disconnected: the landing page cannot reach its own six evidence surfaces, KPI numbers are dead and undated, and no signal chains to root data (an adherence insight links to a page, not to the medication and the missed doses). Second, the console lies under failure: outages render as an empty health record. Third, the manifesto's 'patterns emerge' pillar is only realized on measurements (trend rule-list); symptoms, conditions, and meals still lead with logs, not trajectories, and nothing correlates them. A JARVIS-grade surface would let the owner go headline → concerning signal → exact rows in two keystrokes, always disclose data age, and never present absence of connectivity as absence of history.
audits.redesign_concept: Make /health the spine of the health story and every number on it a door. The left column stays the butler's Voice; the right column becomes a living ledger index — six rows, one per evidence surface, each carrying its own current truth (latest reading + age, 'adherence 86% · next dose 21:00', '2 active conditions', 'last symptom 4d ago · severity 6', 'today 1,540 kcal vs 1,900 avg', '12 notes') and doubling as navigation, mirrored in the sidebar and command palette. Every sub-page leads with trajectory under a single unified time/type scope, and every signal (KPI cell, attention item, condition, insight) deep-links to its pre-filtered evidence with the query already applied. Degraded states speak plainly and are visually unmistakable from emptiness. The result reads calm at 3am and answers 'am I okay, and what changed?' in one glance and one click.
redesign_moves: Ship the ledger index: replace the Overview's lone attention list with a six-row butler index (measurements/medications/conditions/symptoms/meals/research), each row a live status statement + navigation target, mirrored as sidebar nav children and command-palette entries; repoint g-h to /health.

Make every signal a door: KPI cells gain measured-at age + delta and link to /health/measurements?type=X; attention items link to the specific medication/symptom row (anchor or query param), not just the page; condition rows link to their symptoms filtered by condition_id.

Honest degraded mode everywhere: an isError branch on all seven pages rendering a distinct serif 'Couldn't reach the health record — retry' line, and an 'unavailable' red state on the BriefingStatus pill — an outage must never read as an empty record.

One scope to rule the page: collapse the measurements page's three time controls and two type vocabularies into a single page-level type+window scope that drives the trend list, the chart, and the reading log together; apply the same single-scope pattern to meals (list + totals already share, keep it).

Unify the idiom: adopt the quiet mono RowAction/eyebrow language of Medications/Meals across all six sub-pages (one add affordance, one pagination, one header composition, one empty-state voice), and fix the condition status colors so green never decorates an active illness.

Lead nutrition and symptoms with trajectory: DailyTotals leads with daily_avg vs today-so-far; symptoms page gains a deterministic per-symptom 90-day occurrence strip (tiny inline dot-plot per unique symptom) so 'patterns emerge' without any LLM cost.

Grow the insight loop into the pages: surface the same pending insight inline on the sub-page it concerns (e.g. the adherence insight as a one-line banner above the affected medication row) with dismiss/ack writing back to insight_candidates — closing the detect→diagnose→act loop the dashboard doctrine demands.

audits.current_state: /costs ("Costs & Usage") is a workspace-archetype page composing a Today/Last-7-days/custom TimeWindowPicker, four stat cards (total cost, sessions, input/output tokens), a stacked daily-cost bar chart with butler-colored stripes, an inert timeline scrubber, and a per-butler cost table with share bars. Data comes from GET /api/spend (summary) and /api/spend/daily, polled every 60s. The page is orphaned: it appears in no sidebar section (nav-config.ts) and no command-palette entry — the only route in is the Dashboard CostWidget's "View all" link. Meanwhile a second, far richer spend surface (/settings/spend: MTD/forecast/ceiling KPIs, breakdown by butler/model/feature, routing rules, live per-call WS stream) exists in the newer Dispatch design language with no cross-link in either direction.
audits.jarvis_gap: Very far. A JARVIS-grade spend console would open with posture — "MTD $41 of $100 ceiling, tracking to $87, today's burn live, finance up 3x since Tuesday because morning-briefing cron doubled" — and let the owner click any of those clauses to land on the offending schedule or session. This page is a passive accounting readout with fabricated stripes, a dead scrubber, silent-zero failure modes, and no path from any number to evidence; the intelligence that does exist (forecast, ceiling, rules, live per-call stream, top sessions, by-schedule costs — all already built in the backend and half-built at /settings/spend) is scattered across other pages the /costs surface never mentions. It's not even findable in the nav, which disqualifies it as part of the single pane at all.
audits.redesign_concept: One nav-visible "Spend" surface in the Dispatch design language that answers three questions in order: Am I on budget? (MTD-vs-ceiling meter with forecast cone and live today-burn from the WS stream), What changed? (honest per-butler-per-day stacked chart plus a ranked "movers" list of butler/schedule deltas vs the prior window), and Why? (every bar, stripe, butler row, and mover drills to window-scoped top sessions and per-schedule costs, terminating at session detail). Controls — ceiling, routing rules — live on the same surface as the signals they govern, so noticing a spike and capping the schedule that caused it is one continuous motion.
redesign_moves: Merge /costs and /settings/spend into a single 'Spend' page with a sidebar entry and command-palette route; retire the 'Costs & Usage' vocabulary and the legacy card idiom in favor of the Dispatch language already used at /settings/spend.

Make the stripes honest: extend /api/spend/daily to preserve the per-butler day series it already computes and discards (spend.py:700-716), stack real values, and make legend/stripe clicks scope the entire page via the existing butler query param.
Lead with posture, not totals: MTD vs ceiling meter, projected EOM with confidence, and a live today-burn ticker fed by /api/spend/stream; every stat carries its delta vs the previous window.
Replace the dead scrubber with a chart brush: selecting a day or range filters the breakdown table, top sessions, and by-schedule costs to that slice — one gesture from spike to evidence.

Add the missing evidence layer on-page: window-scoped Top Sessions (row -> /sessions/:id) and by-schedule cost table with projected monthly USD, so 'which cron is burning money' is answered without leaving the surface.

Fail honestly: per-butler fetch failures render as an 'n butlers unreported' degraded band (never silent $0.00), sub-cent values render as '<$0.01', and the Dashboard CostWidget sparkline becomes real 7-day data or dies.
Surface anomaly intelligence: a ranked 'movers' strip (butler/schedule spend deltas vs trailing baseline) so the page proactively points at what needs the owner instead of waiting to be scanned.

audits.current_state: /memory is a recently redesigned "house-ledger": an Overture band (display headline "What the house believes.", a templated serif Voice sentence narrating the consolidation pipeline, a 4-cell KPI strip, and a mono pipeline line with a dead-letter fragment), a Band-3 grid pairing one search affordance + three URL-driven registers (Facts ledger, Rules directives, Episodes daybook) against an attention rail (up to five condition rows + recent activity), and a quiet Housekeeping band (retention policies, compaction log, re-embed controls). Detail pages for fact/rule/episode share an editorial DetailSkeleton (eyebrow, state line, KV band, metadata, provenance chain); the fact page carries the surface's only mutations (Confirm/Retract). The design language is unusually disciplined — zero state color on a healthy page, confidence-as-ink dimming, `/`-to-search, URL-round-trippable filters — and is easily the most distinctive, intentional surface in the dashboard.
audits.jarvis_gap: This is the rare Butlers surface with a real point of view — the ink discipline, the templated Voice, zero-red-when-healthy, and URL-honest filters are genuinely close to JARVIS's calm confidence, and the fact→episode→session provenance chain is a true drill-to-evidence path. What keeps it short of an operator console is that the calm is not yet earned: the page cannot tell the owner when it is blind (errors render as health), its loudest alarms terminate in read-only pages with nothing to do about them, and its fleet framing is partly fictional (one butler's embedding pool masquerading as the house total, no per-butler lens despite per-schema pools). JARVIS would say "the relationship butler's write-up failed at 02:14 — here is the session, shall I retry?"; this page says "3 episodes dead-lettered → review" and then goes quiet. Close the honesty and act loops and this becomes the model the rest of the dashboard should copy.
audits.redesign_concept: Keep the house-ledger voice and push it from a beautiful record of belief to a working instrument of belief: every state the page shows is true (loading, degraded, and error narrate themselves in the same Voice as health), every signal in the attention rail lands on exactly the rows that raised it and offers the one action that resolves it (retry the write-up, retire the harmful rule, re-ink the fading fact — inline, arm-then-commit, no modals), and the fleet becomes visible through a butler lens that scopes the whole page to one pool at a time. Memory stops being a place the owner visits to browse and becomes the place the fleet's beliefs get audited and corrected in seconds, keyboard-first, with browser-native links all the way down.
redesign_moves: Make degradation part of the Voice: the Overture's templated sentence gains error/loading/stale templates ("The books are unreachable; last read 14:02.") and every band renders loading/error/empty as three visually distinct truths — the page's calm is then trustworthy, not cosmetic.

Close the Act loop on every rail condition: 'retry consolidation' on dead-lettered/failed episodes, 'retire' commit pill on anti-pattern rule pages, 'confirm' (re-ink) directly on fading ledger rows via a hover/keyboard commit, and make 'write-up overdue' link to the owning consolidation schedule + its last session for root evidence.

Add a butler lens: a ButlerMark pill-row under the search line that scopes stats, registers, rail, and housekeeping to one pool (the per-schema reality) — and rebuild the embeddings surface as per-pool drift rows so re-embed is honest about what it touches.

Go browser-native and keyboard-first on drill-down: real <a> rows (stretched-link pattern), j/k/Enter traversal of the focused register, `g f / g r / g e` register jumps, and rail actions that carry the full predicate (importance_min, status, maturity) so the landing view is exactly the alerted set.

Render provenance as a thread, not links: on any detail page show the chain episode → derived facts → rules inline as a mini-ledger (with belief numerals), so auditing a belief never needs four page loads.

Fix the register arithmetic: server-side anti_pattern pinning, offset-based §NN ordinals, meta.total in search group headers with load-more — the dense surfaces earn their density by being count-honest.

Surface memory into the global command palette: 'memory: search…', 'memory: dead letters', 'memory: retire rule §…' — the fleet's beliefs should be reachable from anywhere in the console, not only from /memory.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/memory/MemoryOverture.tsx:167-192, FactsRegister.tsx:277-282, RulesRegister.tsx:305-310, EpisodesRegister.tsx:347-350, AttentionRail.tsx:259-262, SearchResults.tsx:153-158

audits.current_state: /entities lands on the Plex: a full-bleed radial ego-graph placing contacts on concentric Dunbar rings around the owner, with staleness rendered as desaturation, a client-computed "Worth attention" rail, capacity meters, hover micro-dossiers with 90-day sparklines, drag-to-pin tier overrides, and URL-persisted hop trails into a neighbour mode (predicate-sector fan with confidence-as-opacity and an entity dossier flank). /entities/index is a shadcn-style admin table (filter chips, toolbar search wired to the fuzzy endpoint, bulk gutter, keyboard map, curation queue rail with duplicate-evidence drill into a merge-compare dialog). /entities/concentration is a per-predicate weight balance sheet with tabs, weight bars, provenance marks, and a footer KPI strip. The Plex itself is unusually ambitious and manifesto-literate — the two-axis staleness/confidence rendering and fixed-capacity rings directly encode MANIFESTO.md doctrine.
audits.jarvis_gap: This is the closest surface in the dashboard to a JARVIS pane — the Plex genuinely visualizes doctrine (Dunbar capacity as fixed physics, staleness vs confidence as separate axes) rather than dumping rows. What keeps it short of operator-console grade is the signal-to-action gap and the split brain. Every signal dead-ends at "open record": "Worth attention" tells you Sarah is 40 days overdue but offers no way to act — no "have the butler draft a reach-out", no "schedule a check-in", nothing that discharges the mental labor the manifesto promises to absorb. Worse, the rail is the dashboard's own re-derivation of urgency, not the butler's actual judgment, so the pane shows an approximation of the fleet instead of the fleet itself. Meanwhile the manifesto's other pillars (dates, gifts, loans) are invisible on the landing canvas, and the three tabs fracture into three dialects — an intelligent console (Plex), a CRUD admin panel (Index), and a report (Concentration) — instead of one instrument with three lenses.
audits.redesign_concept: Make the Plex the relationship butler's single instrument and everything else a lens on it. One canvas, one Dispatch dialect, where every signal the butler itself computes — interaction decay, upcoming dates, gift deadlines, duplicate candidates, over-capacity tiers — arrives as a butler-authored attention item with an attached one-keystroke action (center on the person, open the record, ask the butler to draft a reach-out via notify, open the merge compare). Curation (today's Index) becomes a summonable drawer/curation-mode over the same canvas rather than a sibling admin page; Concentration becomes a predicate lens that lights up the corresponding edges on the graph with its balance-sheet in the flank. The owner verifies their social world is tended in one glance, and can go from any faded node to a butler-executed reconnection in under three keystrokes.
redesign_moves: Unify the attention brain: a backend attention-feed endpoint (the same deterministic ranking the relationship-maintenance skill uses, plus upcoming dates and gift deadlines) that both the butler's weekly notify and the rail render — delete the FE's hardcoded cadence tables, and give every rail item actions: center, open, and 'draft reach-out' (queues a butler notify draft for approval).

Collapse the tab family into one canvas: Index becomes a curation drawer summoned from the Plex (`/` or a rail affordance) sharing the Dispatch dialect — rule-rows, bulk gutter, queue chips; duplicate candidates additionally render on the canvas as amber-linked node pairs whose edge opens the compare dialog directly.

Make Concentration a lens, not a page: selecting a predicate highlights those edges and re-weights node emphasis on the live plex, with the balance-sheet (bars, top-3 share, KPI strip) docked in the right flank — and it always opens on the densest predicate, never an empty one.

Fix type honesty end-to-end: carry entity_type through /neighbours into NeighbourPlexNode, hover cards, and sector coloring so organizations, places, and products render as themselves everywhere the graph draws them.

Keyboard-first parity: focus opens the micro-dossier, arrow keys walk within/across rings, Enter opens, `p` pins, `u` unpins with toast-undo, and a `?` overlay documents the keymap identically across canvas, curation drawer, and lens.

First-run and failure honesty: an empty ranking renders an onboarding plex (how the butler fills the graph, one 'tell the butler about someone' entry point) instead of serene empty rings; every load failure gets the same Retry affordance.

Front-load the manifesto's calendar: a thin 'next 14 days' date strip along the top notch of the canvas (birthdays/anniversaries as marks on the ring positions of their people), so Thoughtfulness — the butler's first promise — is the first thing the owner's eye crosses.
