audits.current_state: A 3,470-line single-file page (frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx) rendering one person/org from the relationship graph in two modes: Editorial (default: hero with inline name/type/alias/role editing, PulseStrip stat tiles, 90-day sparkline, delta-since-last-visit banner, canned gloss, an open-by-default "Contact Details" drawer with contact channels + Telegram auth wizard, core dates, latest interactions, profile snapshot, activity timeline, gifts/loans, message threads, grouped facts with on-demand provenance, and a 3x2 curation rail) and Workbench (three-rail dense console: top relations, KPI strip, sortable provenance grid over both fact stores, curation action list, staleness inspector). It has a view-local keyboard map (m/j/k/Esc/e/Shift+Backspace), a single-pair merge-review dialog, and real backend contracts for delta, core dates, activity bins, and fact provenance. The v3 redesign brief's designed depth has genuinely shipped; the composition and truthfulness of what is shown have not caught up.
audits.jarvis_gap: The plumbing is unusually close to JARVIS-grade — real provenance, staleness bands, delta-since-last-visit, merge review with structural diff, a keyboard map — but the composition still reads as a graph-database record inspector, not a briefing about a person. A JARVIS console would open with a synthesized answer ('You last spoke 3 weeks ago, her birthday is in 9 days, one gift idea is stuck at "idea", 2 facts changed since your last look — want me to draft a reach-out?') and let every clause drill to evidence. Today the owner must assemble that answer themselves by scrolling past an open contact-details drawer and a Telegram auth wizard, two facts on the page can outright lie (wrong provenance, cents-as-dollars), several signals dead-end with no drill path, and the page offers zero ways to act on the relationship itself (no log/note/gift/reach-out). The gap is not missing data — it is missing synthesis, truthfulness discipline, and the action layer that turns observation into delegation.
audits.redesign_concept: Recompose the entity page as a person briefing: the first screenful answers, deterministically and without an LLM call, 'how is this relationship and what needs me' — identity band (name, tier, staleness of the whole relationship), a 'since you last looked' strip (delta facts + latest touch per channel, each clause clickable to evidence), a 'coming up' strip (core dates, open loops: unsettled loans, stalled gifts), then the relationship story (timeline) and the knowledge ledger (facts with honest provenance). Everything the owner does *to the record* (curation, merge, contact plumbing) collapses into one command surface; everything the owner does *for the relationship* (log, note, gift, schedule follow-up via the butler's existing tools) becomes the page's primary verbs. Workbench stops being a parallel mode and becomes a slide-over inspector on the same page.
redesign_moves: Flip the fold: hero → 'Since you last looked' (delta banner fused with latest interactions, each row deep-linking to its session/thread) → 'Coming up' (core dates + open loops from gifts/loans) → timeline → facts. Contact Details collapses to a footer drawer; the Telegram wizard moves to the connectors/settings surface entirely.

Add the manifesto's action layer as the page's primary buttons and palette entries: Log interaction, Add note, Gift idea, Schedule follow-up — thin forms that write through the relationship butler's existing MCP-backed endpoints, making this the place connection work happens, not just where it is audited.

Make truthfulness structural: provenance joined by fact id server-side (kill the predicate/content fuzzy match), money formatted from cents at one shared formatter, per-entity duplicate lookup instead of scanning a truncated queue — so nothing on the page can silently lie or silently omit.

Collapse three curation surfaces into one: a single 'Curate' menu (and matching palette commands) with one verb per operation — Confirm identity, Set tier (picker), Merge, Archive (undo toast), Forget (dialog) — and retire the redundant hero/rail/strip duplicates.

One recency vocabulary everywhere: replace the four idioms (Last seen, Last interaction, relative times, staleness badges) with the shared fresh/aging/stale band + one relative timestamp, applied identically in hero, tiles, interactions, and facts.

Make keyboard-first real: autofocus the page root, render shortcut hints, show 'n of m' sibling position scoped to the arrival list, and prefetch the next/previous entity on j/k so stepping through people feels instant.

Demote Workbench from a mode to an inspector: a right slide-over (raw triples grid, KPI strip, staleness inspector) summoned by `t` or a toggle, keeping one stable headline and letting the owner cross-reference briefing and raw knowledge without a layout swap.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:1373 (_provenanceForFact: `?? candidates[0]`)
findings.issue: Editorial fact rows can display another fact's provenance. Matching is by predicate then object/content string equality with a fallback to the first candidate, so when a predicate has multiple facts and content differs (multiple notes, multiple interactions), the reveal shows the wrong src/verified/staleness. The function's own docstring says 'Returns null when no drill row corresponds (no invented provenance)' — the code contradicts it. This misleads the owner on the exact question the surface exists to answer (brief §0: every fact answers 'where did this come from and is it owner-verified').

findings.evidence: Hero 'Mark confirmed' (:3100-3119), PulseStrip DunbarTile dropdown (PulseStrip.tsx:60-161), EditorialCurationRail promote/demote (:2326-2376), WorkbenchActionRail 'Promote'/'Promote tier'/'Demote tier' (:2464-2504), Forget in page actions (:2960) + rail + Shift+Backspace

audits.current_state: The Settings suite is four separately-built pages: a /settings console (attention strip, 4-cell KPI strip, panel grid, QA staffer card, live WS stream with GET fallback), /settings/spend (KPI strip, hand-rolled SVG forecast chart, breakdown bars, drag-to-reorder model-routing rules with a create form, ceiling editor, live spend stream), /settings/permissions (butler-by-permission matrix with reason-required flip modal, 15-entry audit reel, data export/wipe, webhook CRUD with one-time secret reveal), and /settings/models (tier-grouped model catalog with priority steppers, token-usage bars with inline limit editing, verify/test/edit/delete, filter chips). Functionality is genuinely deep — live streams, degraded fallbacks, one-time secret handling — but the four pages were built by four different hands: four page shells, four local Eyebrow copies, three data-fetching styles, and no navigation between siblings.
audits.jarvis_gap: A JARVIS-grade governance console would let the owner answer 'is my fleet spending, permitted, and equipped correctly?' in one glance and change any of it in one keystroke. Today's suite has the raw organs — live spend stream, attention items, a permission matrix, a model catalog — but they are four disconnected rooms with no hallway: numbers repeat and even contradict (two 'MTD' figures from different windows), the matrix silently refuses the owner's most likely action, evidence stops at static pictures (chart and bars you cannot click through to sessions or costs), and destructive controls fire without a net. It reads as four competently-built CRUD admin pages sharing a URL prefix, not one intelligent operator's chamber; the gap is coherence, drill-down continuity, and trust in every displayed number, not missing features.
audits.redesign_concept: Rebuild /settings as the Governance Chamber: one persistent shell where the owner tunes the fleet's autonomy budget — money, models, permissions, credentials — as a single continuous surface. A left sub-nav rail and shared header hold the four domains as tabs of one console; the top of every view is a unified, WS-fed attention queue (over-ceiling, failing models, pending approvals, missing QA credentials) where each item deep-links to — or inlines — the exact control that resolves it; every number on the console appears exactly once, is provably sourced, and is itself the drill-down into its evidence (day → sessions, butler bar → costs, permission flip → audit entry); and every mutation is governed the same way: reason where it matters, confirm or undo where it destroys, and a cross-domain changelog that makes the system's configuration history as inspectable as its behavior.
redesign_moves: Collapse the four bespoke pages into one settings layout route: persistent sub-nav rail (Console · Models · Spend · Permissions · Secrets · QA), one header pattern, one width/grid regime, shared ui/Eyebrow and Page primitives, react-query everywhere — delete the four local Eyebrow copies and the dead Models breadcrumb.

Make attention the spine of the console: a single live queue merging over-ceiling projections, model verification failures, pending approvals, and QA misconfiguration, each row carrying an inline resolution where reversible (raise ceiling, re-verify model) and a deep link where not — replacing the current attention strip + redundant KPI/panel double-decker.

Replace the KPI strip and panel grid with one row of live drill-down tiles: each figure (spend MTD with sparkline+delta, models verified with error count, open approvals, permission overrides active) appears once, from one endpoint, and clicking it lands on the relevant tab pre-filtered to the anomaly.

Wire evidence end-to-end on Spend: hoverable forecast chart (day → cost → top sessions), breakdown bars that navigate to /costs filtered by butler/model, and routing rules showing live proof of effect ('matched 132 dispatches · saved $4.11 this week') so rule ordering becomes an evidence-driven decision.

Permission matrix v2: inherited cells are first-class — click to create an explicit override, with the inheritance source displayed ('inherited: granted · default policy'), an on-surface legend, and each flip linking to its resulting audit entry; the audit reel becomes a cross-settings changelog (permissions, ceilings, rules, models, webhooks) with date-aware timestamps and diff drill-down.

One mutation grammar suite-wide: undo-toast for reversible deletes (rules, webhooks), confirm dialog for irreversible ones (models, wipe), reason capture wherever an autonomous agent's behavior changes — and direct-edit numerics (priority, limits, ceiling) via the same click-to-edit inline pattern everywhere.

Command palette as the fast path: nav entries for every settings sub-route plus governance verbs ('set spend ceiling…', 'verify all models', 'grant <butler> <permission>…', 'add routing rule…'), honoring the dashboard's keyboard-first mandate.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:366-393 (inherited => disabled button; `cell?.inherited ?? true`)

findings.issue: Sub-pages are islands: the only route between Spend, Models, and Permissions is back through the console root via the sidebar; the Models 'breadcrumb' is dead text; Permissions has no upward path at all; none of the sub-routes are in the command palette despite the dashboard's stated keyboard-first scope. findings.evidence: Four page shells: SettingsConsolePage.tsx:540 (bare space-y-6), SettingsSpendPage.tsx:1026 (Page archetype='overview'), SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:1217 (max-w-5xl mx-auto), SettingsModelsPage.tsx:1594 (min-h-screen custom px-7 frame); local Eyebrow re-implemented in all four files despite components/ui/Eyebrow.tsx

findings.evidence: SettingsConsolePage.tsx:254-276 (KpiStrip: spend, approvals, models) vs :325-463 (ModelsPanel, SpendPanel, ApprovalsPanel repeating the same three numbers, ModelsPanel refetching the whole catalog to recount what header_counts already carries)

findings.issue: A full infrastructure-staffer configuration form sits below the fold of the fleet-summary console, styled as a bordered card while everything above is hairline grid, with raw env-var names as user-facing labels. Wrong altitude for the root page and a design-language break.

audits.current_state: /secrets renders the "Direction Passport": a header with a needs-attention headline plus a 3-cell KPI strip (integrations / system / cli), a 296px left spine indexing every credential (needs-hand pinned group, then cli / system / integrations, with search + severity/recency/alpha sort persisted to the URL), and a per-credential page (PageUser / PageSystem / PageCli) with heading band + state plaque, KV band, scopes, what-breaks, probe, audit stamps, and a commit-pill action footer. Data comes live from GET /api/secrets/inventory via TanStack Query (30s stale, 5m refetch), and — contrary to the read-only history — actions ARE genuinely wired: reauthorize/probe/rotate/disconnect for user creds, set/override/delete for system secrets, device-code + api-key flows for CLI runtimes, Google multi-account management with per-account health grant/revoke, and five provider config drawers (HA, OwnTracks, Steam, Spotify, WhatsApp). The visual language (Dispatch: hairlines, mono eyebrows, serif voice, one commit per surface) is executed with unusual discipline.
audits.jarvis_gap: The skeleton of a JARVIS credential console is genuinely here — severity-pinned spine, default focus on the sickest credential, one-click reauth/probe/rotate, per-account Google health grants, honest 501 "not built yet" messaging. What's missing is the evidence layer and the proactive layer. A JARVIS surface answers "is anything about to break, why, and what stops working if it does" from real telemetry; this page answers it with hardcoded strings ("refresh failed · 2d", "Everything else verified within the hour.", "0ms") and permanently-empty audit/scopes/breaks sections whose chrome pretends the data exists. There is no expiry horizon (the 7-day Google test-mode clock is the one exception, buried inside the Google page), no link from a sick credential to the sessions/features it actually broke, and no keyboard path at all. Today it's a beautifully typeset actions panel; the intelligence it displays is partly theater.
audits.redesign_concept: Turn the passport into a credential horizon: the page's organizing axis becomes time-to-breakage, not storage family. The header is a real triage ledger — each needs-hand credential rendered as an attention-list row stating what broke, since when (from real timestamps), which butler features are silent right now (live breaks-catalogue join), and a single commit action inline — so the owner clears the whole queue from the first screenful without ever opening a page. Below the fold, credential pages keep the passport metaphor but every stamp, scope, and probe figure is backed by a queryable source (audit-log join, provider token introspection, measured probe latency) or is absent — the page never prints a value the system didn't observe. The whole surface is keyboard-walkable: slash to search, arrows to leaf through pages like a real passport, palette verbs for every commit action.
redesign_moves: Replace the static header voice with a live triage ledger: one attention-list row per needs-hand credential — real failure age, the butler features currently silent (server-side breaks-catalogue), and the commit action inline — so 'clear the queue' never requires opening a credential page.

Build the expiry horizon: a single mono timeline strip in the header ('google test-mode consent · 3d — codex token · 11d — no other expiries 30d') computed from real expires/refresh timestamps, with the butler proactively re-auth-nagging via notify before anything lapses; today the only countdown that exists is buried inside the Google sub-panel.

Make evidence real or absent: extend /api/secrets/inventory to return issued/expires/scopes/audit joined from the audit log and token introspection, wire the existing breaks-catalogue WhatBreaks component, measure probe latency — and delete every section/column/string the backend cannot back (no more '0ms', 'refresh failed · 2d', '0 events' chrome).

Connect sick credentials to consequences: from a failed credential, deep-link to the actual failed sessions/connector errors it caused ('3 calendar syncs failed since 09:12 → open traces'), turning the what-breaks list from a static catalogue into live blast-radius evidence.

Keyboard-first passport: '/' focuses search, ↑/↓ leafs through spine pages, Enter commits the highlighted primary action, and every action (connect google, rotate ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, probe spotify) registers in the global command palette.

Rebuild the add flow as a provider-first searchable catalog (type 'spo' → Spotify drawer) with 'raw system key' as the power-user escape hatch, killing the system/user/provider family taxonomy that mirrors the database instead of the owner's intent.

Convert all cross-references to instant SPA deep links that keep their promises: audit arrow pre-filtered to the credential's key and always present, connector arrow to the provider's actual detail page, butler names to /butlers/<name> — the drill-down loop should cost one keystroke, not a page reload.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/spine-builder.ts:76-81
findings.issue: Spine sublines are fabricated: every expired user credential shows the hardcoded string "refresh failed · 2d" and every scope_mismatch shows "1 scope missing" regardless of actual failure age or missing-scope count. On a security surface this is invented evidence — it violates the design bar's honesty premise and the page's own no-LLM/verbatim-text charter (pages.tsx header comment).
findings.fix: Derive sublines from real fields (lastVerified/failureTail timestamps, computed missing-scope count) and render nothing when the datum is absent.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/DirectionPassport.tsx:286 (Voice: "Everything else verified within the hour.")
findings.issue: The header voice asserts "Everything else verified within the hour." as a static literal — no code checks any lastVerified timestamp. When probes haven't run for days the page still makes this claim, directly undermining the calm-confidence 'verify at a glance' promise.
findings.fix: Compute the sentence from max(lastVerified) across healthy credentials ("Everything else verified as of 14:21.") or delete it.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-secrets-inventory.ts:184-236 (adapter hardcodes issued/expires/lastUsed=null, scopes/feeds/breaks/audit/usedBy=[]) vs pages.tsx:1236-1360, 1826-1918
findings.issue: The backend inventory returns only state/fingerprint/last_verified/test, yet the page renders full chrome for evidence it can never have: KV band shows "issued —", "expires no expiry", "last used —" on every credential; scopes always read "no scope set"; "stamps · audit" always shows "0 events / No stamps yet."; system "used by" always "nobody yet". The owner cannot distinguish "no history exists" from "not wired" — the spec's Evidence-Over-Value contract is hollow, and the deep-link ActionArrow to /audit-log is gated on audit.length>0 so it never renders.
findings.fix: Extend /api/secrets/inventory to return real issued/expires/scopes and join audit events from the audit log; until then, remove the dead sections and columns entirely (design language rule 4: elements earn their place against state).

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/atoms.tsx:706 + use-secrets-inventory.ts:174 (latencyMs: 0)
findings.issue: ProbeResult always displays "0ms" latency because the adapter (and both mutation merges in pages.tsx:1111-1123, 1734-1746) hardcode latencyMs: 0 — fabricated precision on the one piece of live probe evidence (voice rule: "don't state precision you don't have").
findings.fix: Make latencyMs optional and omit the segment when the server doesn't report it; plumb real latency through the probe endpoints.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/pages.tsx:2338 (envVar) and 2564 (how-to snippet)
findings.issue: The CLI "how to use" snippet builds `$ cli-auth/codex --token ${CLI_AUTH/CODEX_TOKEN}` for real inventory ids like `cli-auth/codex` — the replace only strips hyphens, leaving a slash in the env var name; the rendered command is nonsense the owner might paste.
findings.fix: Sanitize all non-alphanumerics in the env var and render the actual provider invocation (or drop the snippet for cli-auth rows where the runtime manages its own token).

audits.current_state: A single-route page (/education) that loads active mind maps, auto-selects the first, and offers a curriculum dropdown plus three tabs: Curriculum (ReactFlow DAG of concepts with a node detail side panel, status/abandon actions, quiz history), Reviews (pending spaced-repetition reviews across all active maps grouped Overdue/Today/This Week/Later), and Analytics (four stat cards, 30-day mastery area chart, cross-topic bar chart, struggling-concepts list). Data is real and live-polled (15-60s intervals via TanStack Query), with a Request Curriculum dialog that POSTs a curriculum request the butler processes asynchronously. It is a competent read-mostly viewer of the education butler's data model, but it does not surface the butler's teaching flow state machine, has two actively misleading displays, and offers almost no drill-down from signal to evidence.
audits.jarvis_gap: This surface is a competent data viewer, not an operator console — roughly the midpoint between CRUD admin panel and JARVIS. The gap is threefold. First, agency is invisible: the education butler is a live agent moving through a five-phase teaching state machine, yet the page shows only its data artifacts (maps, scores, timestamps) and never the agent itself — no phase, no pending work, no 'last session', no next scheduled action, so the owner cannot verify at a glance that the tutor is actually tutoring. Second, signals don't convert to action: overdue reviews, struggling concepts, and review rows are either dead-ends or literally dead clicks, and there is no path from any number to the session evidence that produced it. Third, honesty gaps (fabricated mastery percentages, errors dressed as empty states, dark-mode illegibility) erode exactly the calm confidence a JARVIS pane exists to provide. The bones are good — real DAG visualization, real spaced-repetition data, live polling — but the page reads the butler's database instead of standing in for the butler.
audits.redesign_concept: Turn the page into the owner's learning cockpit: a top strip that answers 'is my tutor working and what needs me' in one glance (due/overdue reviews, current teaching phase per curriculum, next frontier concept, last butler session), above a full-height, legend-bearing knowledge map that is the manifesto's 'learning territory' made real — every node, review entry, struggling concept, and stat is a live door that opens the same node dossier (mastery history, quiz transcript with evaluator notes, next review, link to the originating butler session), and every promise the butler makes (a requested curriculum, a scheduled review) is visible as a tracked, in-progress commitment until it resolves.
redesign_moves: Add a 'tutor status' hero strip fed by useTeachingFlows + pending reviews: per active curriculum show phase (Diagnosing/Planning/Teaching/Quizzing/Reviewing), overdue+due-today count, next frontier concept, and last-activity time — with one-click actions ('start review now', 'continue teaching') that trigger the butler, closing the Detect→Act loop on the first screenful.

Make the concept map the full-height centerpiece with an always-visible legend, theme-token colors, and a fullscreen toggle; replace the curriculum dropdown with a portfolio rail of curriculum cards (progress ring, phase chip, due count) so switching topics is one glance and one click instead of a blind Select.

Unify all drill-down into a single node dossier drawer reachable from anywhere — graph node, review row, struggling concept, quiz entry — showing mastery trajectory sparkline, full quiz transcript, SM-2 schedule, and a deep link to the butler session that taught/quizzed it (root evidence).

Ship honest state everywhere: real mastery scores in the review list (extend the pending-reviews API), a distinct error state with retry (never the empty state), skeleton loading, positive healthy-state copy ('no struggling concepts'), and a visible pending-request card the moment a curriculum is requested.

Replace the Analytics tab with an embedded 'momentum' band under the hero (velocity trend, retention rate, estimated completion, cross-topic portfolio) so the weekly-digest numbers the manifesto promises are ambient rather than hidden behind a tab.

Register the page in the keyboard layer: command-palette entries for 'Request curriculum', per-curriculum jump, 'open reviews due', and j/k node navigation in the graph; make every expandable row a real button.

Add a review-forecast calendar (next 14+ days of scheduled reviews as a density strip) so the owner can see the spaced-repetition engine breathing — the strongest possible 'the system is working' signal for this butler.

audits.current_state: /chronicles is an editorial-archetype retrospective archive: a two-column above-the-fold layout (left: date stepper + 44px Display headline + serif voice paragraph sourced from the day-close Tier-2 cache; right: attention list, 4-cell KPI strip, recent-days index) over a below-the-fold drilldown panel (source-state badge strip, time scrubber, hand-rolled SVG Gantt swimlane by life-lane, floating map minimap, streak callouts, stacked-bar and pie aggregates, and a click-to-open EpisodeDrawer with linked events, correction history, and a rate-limited "Explain this episode" LLM button). The selected day is URL state (?date=YYYY-MM-DD) clamped to [earliest_date, yesterday] in the owner's timezone; settled days never poll, and navigation never triggers an LLM call. Loading/error/empty states are handled per-widget; privacy (normal/sensitive/restricted) is enforced consistently in Gantt bars, tooltips, and the drawer.
audits.jarvis_gap: The chronicler's manifesto promises an interrogable memory — "what did I do yesterday?", "when did I last go running?", corrections that never get lost — and the backend genuinely has the pieces (day-close bundles, explain dispatch, correction overrides, provenance on every row). The page, however, is a read-only daily report with a debug annex: the voice paragraph is disconnected prose (no sentence links to its evidence), the one AI drill-down writes its answer somewhere the UI never looks, corrections are display-only, retrospective questions are unanswerable, and moving through time — the page's entire axis — is a mouse-only, skeleton-flashing slog with no way to jump to an arbitrary day or see patterns across days. A JARVIS-grade console would let the owner ask the Chronicler questions, click any claim in the narrative to see the evidence that backs it, correct the record in place, and read a month of life-rhythm at a glance. Today's page shows what one day looked like; it does not yet let the owner converse with, verify, or correct their own history.
audits.redesign_concept: The queryable memoir: one continuous, keyboard-native archive where the Chronicler's narrative, its evidence, and the correction loop are a single surface. The voice paragraph becomes the index into the day — every sentence is a citation that highlights its Gantt bars and map trail on hover and opens the episode on click. A month heatmap (coloured by state_class) replaces the recent-days list so any day is one keystroke away and life-rhythm is legible at a glance; arrow keys step days instantly over kept-warm data. An explicit ask-bar routes retrospective questions through the token-bounded bundle machinery and renders answers inline with provenance, and the episode drawer closes the loop: real title, rendered explanation prose, and an in-place "correct this" that exercises the override layer the manifesto promises. Aggregates stop restating the day and start contextualizing it — this day against the owner's normal week.
redesign_moves: Evidence-linked narrative: render the day-close prose with per-sentence provenance refs (already stored in tier2_cache.provenance_refs); hovering a sentence highlights the cited Gantt bars/map segment, clicking opens the EpisodeDrawer — the Voice becomes the drill-down index instead of decoration.

Ask-the-Chronicler bar: a single input on the page ("when did I last go running?") that dispatches a token-bounded Tier-2 query against the day/range bundle and renders the cited answer inline — the manifesto's headline capability, currently chat-only, lands on the single pane.

Month heatmap + keyboard time travel: replace RecentDaysIndex with a GitHub-style calendar heatmap coloured by state_class/total hours for one-click jump to any day; bind arrow keys to day-stepping and t to latest, backed by keepPreviousData plus adjacent-day prefetch so every step renders in one frame.

Close the drawer loop: title the drawer with the episode's real title, fetch and display the explain prose with a cache-age pill (fixing the dead-end LLM path), and add inline correction submission (start/end/title/privacy/tombstone) over the existing override API.

Comparative context band: swap the single-bar stacked chart and pie for a 7/30-day lane-hours band with the selected day highlighted and click-to-navigate, plus a lane table with deltas vs the owner's median day — answering "was this normal?" instead of restating the pie.

One honest freshness surface: a doctrine status pill (llm · cached 2h / templated / stale) beside the date that is itself the regenerate action (wired to the existing day-close refresh endpoint), and a single Refresh that invalidates every widget in view including episodes and the briefing.

Coverage-aware source strip: translate adapter identifiers to friendly lane-coloured names and reframe as evidence coverage for the selected day ("Location gap 14:00–17:00", "Calendar quiet"), so the owner can calibrate how much to trust the day's reconstruction.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/EpisodeDrawer.tsx:88-153 (ExplainButton) + roster/chronicler/api/router.py:826-863 (EpisodeExplainResponse returns only episode_id/cache_key/cache_built_at)
findings.issue: "Explain this episode" is a dead-end LLM spend that actively misleads: the POST dispatches a Tier-2 LLM session and writes the prose to tier2_cache, but no GET endpoint or frontend path ever reads episode_explain:{id} back; the drawer's onSuccess shows "Episode explanation refreshed." though nothing visible changed anywhere. findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ChroniclesPage.tsx:218 (loading={!data && !isError}) + frontend/src/hooks/use-chronicles-briefing.ts:33-43 (per-date queryKey, no placeholderData)

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/SourceStateBadgeStrip.tsx:46-48 (getLaneConfig keys LANE_TAXONOMY by row.source_name) vs src/butlers/chronicler/contracts.py:31-60 (source_name values are core.sessions, google_calendar.completed, spotify.session_summary, …)

findings.evidence: ChroniclesPage.tsx:226-263 (two icon buttons are the only navigation) + RecentDaysIndex.tsx (short list of recent days only)

For a page whose purpose-and-single-pane doc promises "keyboard-first navigation for operational speed", the primary axis of the page is mouse-only (design-bar bias 7 and Definition-of-Done Findable).

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:184-197 — AggregateStackedBar fed a single-day window next to AggregatePieChart of the same window

audits.current_state: The /qa suite is the QA staffer's operator surface. /qa is a dossier shell: sticky filter bar (severity + time range + force-patrol + its own theme toggle), an editorial header ("What the staff caught and fixed"), a 4-cell KPI strip, and a two-pane body — a 320px case rail and a case dossier with a claim-anchored diagnosis blurb, hover-linked evidence log, counter-evidence, PR panel with diff preview, and a patrol journal. /qa/investigations is a filterable flat case index reusing CaseList; /qa/investigations/:id mounts the same CaseDossier with breadcrumb chrome; /qa/patrols/:id shows one patrol's findings and dispatched investigations. Data polls every 30s via TanStack Query hooks.
audits.jarvis_gap: The dossier core is genuinely JARVIS-grade in concept — claim-anchored diagnosis with hover-linked evidence, counter-evidence verdicts, and a decision journal is exactly 'instant drill-down from signal to root evidence.' But the suite around it fails the operator-console test in three ways. First, it can't establish calm confidence: the overview hides the very signals (patrol heartbeat, circuit breaker, missing GH token) its own API returns and its manifesto promises to surface — you cannot glance and know the patrol loop is alive. Second, drill paths are broken in both directions: KPIs and escalation counts are inert, patrols are orphaned routes reachable only via the butler-detail tab, and the 'Proposed fix' panel misreports in-flight cases as escalated — the single pane sometimes lies. Third, there is zero keyboard surface (no j/k rail navigation, no palette verbs for dismiss/retry/force-patrol), so an operator moves at mouse speed through what should be a triage loop. It's an excellent case reader wrapped in an incomplete console.
audits.redesign_concept: Turn /qa into the staff's case room: a single surface whose top edge is a living heartbeat (last patrol 4m ago · next in 6m · breaker OK · credentials OK, with a red remediation banner the moment any of those degrade), whose first content is a 'Needs you' lane — escalated cases and open PRs awaiting the human merge seat, because 'humans remain in the merge seat' is the product's one owner-facing chore — and whose everything-else is the existing dossier, now fully evidence-linked: every KPI opens its filtered case set, every journal tick opens its patrol, every patrol finding opens its case, and every case is one keystroke away. The healthy state is not emptiness but verified quiet: 'No open cases. 143 clean patrols this week.'
redesign_moves: Heartbeat header: replace the port/model caption with staffer_status, last/next patrol countdown, circuit-breaker and credentials state from the summary the API already returns; tripped breaker or missing GH token renders a red banner with a one-click remediation link (/secrets), per the manifesto's failure-mode table.

'Needs you' lane above the rail: escalated cases and PRs awaiting human review pinned first with merge/dismiss affordances — the owner's only real job in this loop — and make the KPI 'active/escalated' numbers deep-link into it.

Absorb patrols into the surface: a patrol pulse strip (last ~24 patrols as clean/dispatched/error ticks with duration) linking to patrol detail, killing the orphaned /qa/patrols route problem and giving the journal's 'tick' entries somewhere to go; fold /qa/investigations into /qa with URL-persisted filters so there is one canonical case index.

Fix the truth layer: stage-aware PR panel copy (never 'Escalated to user' for an in-flight case), one timezone across dossier and journal, distinct not-found vs unreachable errors, and a single severity vocabulary with visible labels.

Keyboard-first triage loop: j/k through the case rail, Enter to open, d dismiss, r retry, p force patrol, plus EntityFinder/palette entries for 'QA: escalated cases' and 'Force patrol' — the suite currently has zero shortcut surface despite the shell shipping a command palette.
Make force patrol feel alive: drop window.confirm, fire optimistically, and stream the new patrol's journal ticks into view as they land instead of waiting for the 30s poll.

Strip duplicated chrome: remove the page-local theme toggle and reconcile the page's sticky bars with the shell header so /qa composes like every other page instead of carrying its own mini-app frame.

audits.current_state: The ingestion console is a freshly redesigned four-route surface (/ingestion timeline ledger, /connectors roster, /filters pipeline, /connectors/:type/:id detail) built on new Dispatch primitives (DispatchLayout/Header/Surface, IngestionSubNav) per docs/redesigns/ingestion-design-language.md, with the legacy tabbed page behind a kill-switch flag. The timeline is a genuinely dense hour-grouped ledger with URL-backed drawer (sessions flamegraph → /sessions/:id drill-down, raw payload, replays), saved views (built-in + backend-persisted custom), server-side status/channel/search filters, bulk replay with 409-aware deselect, and a window rollup band. Connectors is a hairline roster with attention strip, dormant catalog, and a two-zone editorial detail page; Filters renders a five-gate funnel diagram with real rule CRUD, priority senders, and channel defaults. States are mostly honest: degraded-metrics envelopes render "metrics unavailable," empty sessions get a reasoned serif explanation, estimated gate counts are marked "~/est."
audits.jarvis_gap: This is the closest surface in the app to an operator's console — it has real drill-down (row → drawer → session flamegraph → session page), honest degraded states, and a coherent editorial density. But a JARVIS ingestion pane is a living instrument: it streams (this one polls at 30s with no new-event affordance), its health signal is trustworthy at 3am (the Live badge can lie indefinitely), every anomaly is a door (the landing page's attention items are dead spans), and it leads with judgment ("gmail has been silent 6h, that's unusual") rather than a neutral chronological tape the owner must interpret. Today the console shows what happened; it does not yet notice, prioritize, or speak. The pieces — attention strip, rollup, error views, serif Voice — exist but are arranged as peers instead of a triage hierarchy, and the two visual dialects (Dispatch vs leftover shadcn/Tailwind) mean it can't yet be handed to the rest of the app as the reference language without laundering.
audits.redesign_concept: Make /ingestion the house's seismograph: a page that opens with the system's own one-line judgment of the pipe ("All channels live. 412 signals today, 3 need you.") above a full-window density band, then the ledger as evidence beneath it. Every colored pixel is a door — attention items, gate counts, flame-strip hours, roster rows all navigate to the pre-filtered evidence in one click or keystroke — and every signal is honest by construction: freshness decays on a clock, histograms cover the whole window not the loaded page, and unknown metadata renders as unknown. One dialect (Dispatch tokens, three state colors, pill controls) everywhere, so this page graduates from redesign experiment to the canonical grammar the rest of the dashboard extends.
redesign_moves: Lead with triage, not tape: replace the static header description with a Voice line composed from live state (connector incidents + error/replay-failed counts + freshness), each clause a link to its pre-filtered view; when quiet, one serif-italic sentence — the ledger becomes the second screenful element, not the first.

Make it a live tape: stream or fast-poll new events with a pinned '3 new events ↑' affordance instead of silent 30s refetches; drive the Live badge from a decaying clock and an unfiltered heartbeat so it can never show stale green.

Wire the shipped histogram endpoint into a full-window master density band at the top of the ledger (hour buckets colored by error share, click-to-zoom into an hour), replacing the per-page flame strips and fixing hour-header counts.

Every signal is a door: attention-strip items link to connector detail everywhere (one shared component), roster rows are fully clickable and keyboard-focusable, and each gate numeral in the filters funnel deep-links to /ingestion pre-filtered to that gate's outcome statuses.

One dialect: port the timeline toolbar, status chips, bulk bar, and save-view dialog onto Dispatch primitives (square mono pills, token colors, hairlines); fold RowStatus/StatusBadge into a single status component with one vocabulary and three state colors; delete the flag-off legacy pages and root-level legacy components (ConnectorCard, ConnectorsTab, FiltersTabContent, ConnectorsListPage).

Keyboard-first power loop: '/' focuses search, j/k walks rows, Enter opens the drawer, r replays, 1/2/3 set range, and saved views register in the command palette — the ten-th-use path never touches the mouse.

Unify connector detail into one shell whose loading state is a skeleton of itself, with backend-sourced transport kind and purpose gloss (extend the connector catalog) so the Voice always says something true the owner didn't already read in the adjacent column.

audits.current_state: /system is a read-only "ownership facts" board: eight polling cards (version, uptime, DB size, security posture, insight-delivery counts, backups, owner-only egress catalog, per-butler heartbeats) laid out in a 3-column grid, followed by a full-width react-flow "Ecosystem Topology" graph placing the switchboard at center, butlers in a right semicircle, connectors in a left semicircle, with clickable nodes navigating to /butlers/:name or connector detail. Every tile handles loading/error/empty states honestly (no faked data — DbSize even omits its sparkline rather than fabricate it), and data refreshes on 30–120s intervals via TanStack Query. There are no actions anywhere on the page; it is purely detect-layer.
audits.jarvis_gap: Substantial. The page is honest and complete as a facts board — every tile shows real data with real empty states, which puts it above a fake dashboard — but it is a passive, read-only poster, not an operator console. JARVIS-grade means the page opens with a spoken-quality verdict ("everything nominal" / "two things need you"), the topology is the living nervous-system map with one authoritative liveness truth and hover-to-inspect drill-down, and every anomaly carries its remediation inline. Today the owner must visually scan eight equal cards, mentally reconcile two conflicting health encodings, and leave the page to act on anything it reports. It also partially duplicates the home triage cockpit's fleet-health job (heartbeats, butler status) while underplaying its unique, manifesto-aligned job: sovereignty — proving "your instance, your data, your butlers" (version, backups, egress, security posture) at a glance.
audits.redesign_concept: Make /system the sovereignty-and-substrate console: the one page that proves the owner still owns a healthy machine. It opens with a single computed verdict line — "Instance healthy: v0.4.2, up 12 days, backed up 3h ago, no insecure defaults, all 9 butlers beating, data left the house via 3 known services" — or a ranked problem list when anything is off. Below it, the live topology graph is the hero: theme-native, legend-equipped, powered by one canonical liveness model, where hovering any node shows heartbeat age, active sessions, and last activity, and clicking drills to root evidence. Ownership facts (version/uptime/DB/backup/egress/security) compress into a dense fact rail where every number is a door — to the audit log, the butler, the failing insight, or the remediation setting — and every degraded data source announces itself instead of vanishing.
redesign_moves: Lead with a computed verdict banner synthesizing all tile data already on the client (posture booleans, backup recency, stale-heartbeat count, failed insights) into one all-clear line or a ranked, clickable problem list — the tiles become elaboration, not the message.

Promote the topology graph to the hero and make it the single source of fleet truth: merge heartbeat age + status into one liveness model shared with any list view, restyle with design-system tokens for both themes, add a legend, add hover cards (heartbeat age, active sessions, port, last session), and fold the separate Butler Heartbeats card into a list-view toggle of the same model.

audits.current_state: The app shell is a fixed left sidebar (expanded 240px or 56px icon rail, mobile sheet) with three sections (Main, Dedicated Butlers, Telemetry) totaling ~19 destinations, butler-aware item filtering, live badge counts for QA escalations and pending approvals, and a footer dot aggregating fleet health plus today's spend. A slim header carries URL-derived breadcrumbs, a search button, and a theme toggle. Two separate command overlays coexist: a legacy shadcn CommandPalette (opened by "/" and the header button; searches nav pages, butlers, and server-side entities/contacts/sessions/state) and a cmdk EntityFinder (opened by Cmd/Ctrl+K; entity-first with preview pane, Tab-to-hop, and owner-pinned empty state). g+key chords cover 11 destinations, documented in a mouse-only "?" floating dialog.
audits.jarvis_gap: The shell is a competent directory, not an operator's console. A JARVIS-grade shell would lead with attention — what needs the owner right now — and let every signal be grabbed and pulled to root evidence; here the attention surface is two tiny badges and an unclickable footer dot, the command surface is split across two overlapping palettes neither of which can execute a single verb, and a third of the operational surfaces (costs, approval rules, groups) are invisible to both nav and search. Keyboard speed exists in fragments (g-chords, Tab-to-hop, cmdk finder with preview — genuinely good bones) but the fragments contradict each other and their own documentation, and shortcuts die whenever focus is in an input. The gap is not missing features; it is coherence: one command registry, one palette, signals that drill down, and a sidebar organized by what needs the owner rather than by module inventory.
audits.redesign_concept: Collapse the shell around a single omnipresent command spine: one Cmd+K palette (cmdk, the EntityFinder's DNA) that fuzzy-matches verbs, destinations, and entities from one registry that also drives the sidebar, g-chords, tooltips, and the help sheet — so nothing can drift and nothing can hide. The sidebar inverts from module inventory to attention hierarchy: a live 'Needs you' cluster at top (approvals, escalations, reauth, failing butlers — each count a direct link into the filtered queue), domains in the middle, telemetry collapsed below; the footer status dot becomes a fleet-health popover with per-butler drill-down and a spend link. audits.current_state: The app has a genuinely sophisticated token layer (frontend/src/index.css: OKLCH light/dark parity, semantic severity/permanence/tier/category sets, type/spacing/motion tokens) and a settled written doctrine (about/heart-and-soul/design-language.md plus the "Dispatch" language doc duplicated as docs/redesigns/ingestion-design-language.md and secrets-design-language.md, which are byte-identical). In code, however, the product renders in at least three coexisting visual worlds: (1) the legacy shadcn baseline (system-ui body font, rounded-xl shadow cards, filled Buttons/Badges, raw Tailwind palette colors) covering roughly half the pages; (2) the Dispatch dialect via shared ui/ primitives (Eyebrow, Voice, Display, Pill, StateDot, ButlerMark, Row) used by Dashboard/Health/EntityDetail; and (3) per-redesign private re-implementations of the same Dispatch atoms (components/ingestion/dispatch/, components/secrets/passport/atoms.tsx, components/butler-detail/atoms.tsx, plus local Eyebrow functions in three Settings pages and QA pages). Dark-primary is real (useDarkMode defaults dark) and tabular-numeral discipline is widespread (~112 files), but chart color plumbing is broken app-wide and status hues have fractured into token, Tailwind-palette, and hex variants.
audits.jarvis_gap: A JARVIS-grade console has one unmistakable voice: the owner should never be able to tell which subcontractor built which room. Today the dashboard is visibly three products — a stock shadcn admin panel (system-ui, shadowed cards, emerald/amber Tailwind classes), the Dispatch editorial surfaces (Inter Tight, hairline rules, serif Voice), and per-redesign private forks of Dispatch that are already drifting from each other. The bones are unusually good — a real OKLCH token system with light/dark parity, a settled dark-primary doctrine, a written language with teeth, tnum discipline, an honest ButlerMark identity system — which means the gap is not vision but enforcement: the language is opt-in, the primitives are copy-pasted instead of imported, and the charts (the very surfaces an operator trusts most) render with literally broken color plumbing. Calm confidence at a glance requires that green means one thing, that a butler's hue is genuinely its identity, and that the numbers and trends the owner scans nightly are painted in the palette that was tuned for a dim room — none of which holds yet.
audits.redesign_concept: Make Dispatch the only language and make it unforgeable. One design-language document, one primitive kit under components/ui/ (Eyebrow, Voice, Display, Pill, StateDot, ButlerMark, Row, KpiStrip, AttentionList, Section, Time), one Page shell that every route must mount — and machinery, not discipline, holding the line: lint rules that ban hsl(var(), raw status-palette classes, local primitive re-declarations, and hex in JSX; a body typeface set once; a chart layer that consumes the tuned --chart tokens and state semantics through a single helper. The shadcn kit survives only as restyled plumbing (dialogs, dropdowns, inputs retuned to Dispatch radii, motion, and surfaces), never as a visible dialect. The result reads like a single sheet of paper from a private bank: paper-warm or near-black surfaces, type-and-rule hierarchy, hue appearing only where it means something — a butler's mark, a state that demands attention, a chart series.
redesign_moves: Fix the chart layer in one stroke: repo-wide replace hsl(var(--X)) with var(--X), route every categorical series through --chart-1..5 / butlerHueVar via one shared series-color helper, reserve red/amber/green for state meaning inside charts, and set recharts text to the mono token with tnum — then screenshot-verify every chart in dark mode.

Flip the body font to var(--font-sans) (Inter Tight) globally and restyle the shadcn primitives themselves — Card to the flat Dispatch surface (hairline border, no shadow, 4-6px radius), Button to pill/commit forms, tooltip instant, sheet/dialog at duration-base ease-out-quart — so unmigrated pages inherit the language for free instead of waiting for page-by-page rewrites.

Enforce by machine: eslint rules banning hsl(var(, text/bg-{green,emerald,amber,red,yellow,blue}-N status classes, local declarations of Eyebrow/Voice/Mono/Display, and 6-digit hex in JSX (chart-token and typed-primitive exemptions encoded); delete the six duplicate atom sets by re-exporting from components/ui/.

Unify the shell: fold DispatchHeader into <Page> as the editorial/dispatch header variant, migrate HealthOverviewPage and SecretsPage onto <Page>, and settle the H1 question at two tiers exactly (standard + Display) — retiring ingestion's third tier.

Make butler hue a real identity: expand the categorical ramp to cover the full roster without collisions, regenerate the doc's mapping table from ButlerMark.KNOWN_BUTLERS (single source of truth), and split non-butler entity coloring onto a separate muted ramp so a colored squircle always means a butler.

Consolidate doctrine to one file: merge the Dispatch doc's binding sections into about/heart-and-soul/design-language.md (or one docs/design-language.md), delete the two identical per-redesign copies and the pr/overview strays, and resolve the two open contradictions it currently carries (skeleton-pulse vs animate-pulse loading; light-mode state-color values).

Adopt the attention-tint + StateDot + serif-italic-empty trio as the app-wide state vocabulary: sweep the 47 raw-palette status files onto var(--red/--amber/--green), convert state-colored background fills to the sanctioned tint pattern, and collapse the three empty-state treatments into EmptyState's two documented registers.

audits.current_state: The dashboard is a React 19 + TanStack Query SPA with sane cache defaults (global staleTime 30s, retry 1 in frontend/src/lib/query-client.ts) and pervasive interval polling (15s-5min scattered across ~40 hooks) as its freshness mechanism. Three bespoke WebSocket channels exist (approvals, spend, settings-console) that push events and invalidate query caches, but every core fleet-monitoring surface — butlers, sessions, timeline, notifications, issues, ingestion — polls. Mutations (~247 useMutation sites) almost universally follow invalidate-on-success; only issue dismiss/undismiss and one ApprovalsPage path are optimistic. Skeleton primitives exist and are used on key pages; a command palette gives instant client-side nav results with debounced server search.
audits.jarvis_gap: JARVIS never shows a spinner for something it already knew, and never waits for permission to update — state changes appear the moment they happen, the owner's actions take effect the instant they're expressed, and the next thing the owner will look at is already loaded. This dashboard is a competent poll-and-refetch console: honest, cache-backed, but structurally reactive. Fleet state is 15–60 seconds stale by design, every write is gated on two server round trips before the UI believes it, drill-downs start from a blank skeleton even when half the answer is already in cache, and pagination erases what the owner was reading. The ingredients for the JARVIS feel already exist in the codebase — three working WebSocket channels, one correct optimistic-mutation implementation, skeleton primitives, an instant-client-results command palette — but each was built once for one surface and never made the default. The gap is not capability, it is generalization: the system's best patterns are exceptions instead of policy.
audits.redesign_concept: Make the dashboard event-driven and presumptuous: one multiplexed fleet event stream (the daemon already emits sessions, notifications, ingestion, approvals, spend) drives targeted react-query cache patches so every surface is live-by-default and polling survives only as a five-minute safety net; every mutation that almost always succeeds applies locally in the same frame and rolls back loudly on failure; every list keeps its previous rows through any filter or cursor change; every drill-down opens pre-seeded from the summary row the owner clicked while the remainder streams in. The owner should never be able to catch the dashboard not knowing something the daemon already knows, and should never wait to see their own action reflected.
redesign_moves: Build the fleet event bus: generalize use-approvals-stream.ts into a single /api/events WebSocket multiplexing session/notification/ingestion/issue/approval/spend kinds, mapped declaratively to query-key patches or invalidations; demote all 15-60s polling to a 5-minute reconciliation sweep and make the shell's Live indicator reflect actual socket health.

Make optimism the default: extract use-issues.ts's onMutate/rollback pattern into a shared useOptimisticMutation helper and sweep all ~247 mutation sites, classifying each as optimistic (toggles, acks, dismissals, renames) or honest-pending (trigger session, replay, secrets) — with loud toast+restore rollback on failure.

Never blank a list: placeholderData:(prev)=>prev plus an isFetching dim overlay as the enforced default for every cursor/filter-keyed list query (sessions, timeline, ingestion, notifications, audit log), replacing skeleton-on-repage everywhere.

Anticipate drill-downs: hover/focus on any row prefetches its detail query, and detail drawers/pages seed placeholderData from the cached list row so they open instantly populated (SessionDetailDrawer first — it's the hottest Diagnose path).

Collapse the /butlers N+1: one GET /api/butlers/board endpoint returning status, eligibility, heartbeat, cost, max_concurrent, and hourly buckets per row, replacing the 2-queries-per-butler waterfall in use-butler-status-board.ts.

Split and preload routes: lazy-load heavy leaf routes (PlexPage/@xyflow, Chronicles, Calendar, QA) with sidebar hover-preload, keeping the hot core eager — first daily open gets fast, route hops stay instant.

Harden the transport: apiFetch accepts an AbortSignal with a 15s timeout default and hooks forward TanStack's signal, so filter churn cancels dead requests and a wedged daemon produces an actionable error state instead of an eternal skeleton.

audits.current_state: The dashboard's accessibility posture is a patchwork of genuinely excellent pockets and structurally broken assurance. Strong: Radix-based dialog/sheet/dropdown primitives with focus traps and sr-only close labels; correct `inert` usage on collapsed sidebar submenus (typed via src/inert.d.ts); StateDot with role=img + aria-label and status dots always paired with words; a remarkably keyboard-conscious CalendarWorkspacePage (real buttons for every grid cell/event, keyboard-activation fallback via evt.detail===0, one-click Undo ghost); cmdk-backed EntityFinder with proper listbox semantics; a dedicated usePrefersReducedMotion hook used in 3 components. Weak: the two *.a11y.test.tsx files run axe against hand-written stub DOM rather than the shipped components, there is no eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, color contrast is verified nowhere (and measurably fails in the light theme), and the densest operator surface — the ingestion timeline ledger — is a div-with-onClick construction that screen-reader and keyboard users cannot fully operate.
audits.jarvis_gap: A JARVIS-grade console must be operable at reflex speed with eyes anywhere — which means keyboard paths and announcements are the interface, not a compliance layer. Today the surface is maybe 60% of the way there in the pockets that were designed deliberately (calendar grid, sidebar, Radix primitives, EntityFinder) and near 0% in the assurance layer: the axe suite tests replicas of components, contrast was never actually measured (and fails where the design language leans hardest — tiny mono type in dim/amber), and the single hottest drill-down loop (ledger row → event drawer) drops keyboard and screen-reader users at both hops: the row is an unsemantic div, and the drawer opens silently with no focus hand-off and no Escape. The gap is not effort — enormous care is visible — it is that accessibility was implemented per-bead by different workers with no shared enforced grammar, so quality varies wildly per surface and nothing stops regression.
audits.redesign_concept: Make accessibility a property of the design system, not of individual pages: one enforced 'operator grammar' of five interaction primitives — RowLink (navigating row), DisclosureRow (expanding row), SubNav/tabs, Palette (cmdk-based), and Drawer (focus-managed disclosure) — each shipped once in components/ui/ with correct roles, keyboard maps, focus choreography, and live announcements baked in, and every dense surface (ingestion ledger, facts register, status board, calendar lanes) recomposed onto them. Underneath, a contrast-locked token palette whose WCAG ratios are asserted by a pure-math unit test in both themes, an eslint jsx-a11y + design-token gate that makes raw click-handler divs and unsafe text colors unshippable, and axe running against the real routed pages. The result: the JARVIS console is fully drivable blind — arrow through the ledger, Space to expand, hear the drawer arrive, Escape back — and no future fleet worker can silently ship below that floor.
redesign_moves: Ship a DisclosureRow + RowLink primitive pair in components/ui/ (role, Enter+Space, aria-expanded/aria-controls, focus ring, aria-hidden chevrons, ≥24px action targets) and recompose TimelineTab LedgerRow, FactsRegister, RulesRegister, and StatusBoardCell onto them — one fix, four surfaces, and the pattern is enforced for every future ledger.

Give the event drawer real disclosure choreography: focus moves to the drawer heading on expand, Escape collapses and returns focus to the row, a polite live region announces 'event detail open — 3 sessions'; rebuild its internal tab bar and the four other hand-rolled tab bars on the Radix tabs primitive.

Burn the fake assurance layer: delete the stub-DOM a11y tests, run axe against the real ButlersPage/TimelineTab/CalendarWorkspacePage with mocked data, add eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y to the CI eslint job, and add a token-contrast unit test (oklch→sRGB→WCAG ratio, both themes) so the palette can never regress below AA unmeasured.

Contrast-lock the palette: darken light --dim, mint a text-safe amber token separate from fill/border amber, extend the existing design-token eslint guard to forbid --amber/--red/--dim as text color outside approved tokens, and re-express 'fading' facts with a readable grey plus a non-color cue.

Unify the launchers: rebuild CommandPalette on cmdk (combobox/listbox/aria-activedescendant + live result-count announcements) and host EntityFinder inside the Radix Dialog so both keyboard-first surfaces trap focus, close on Escape, and restore focus — identical muscle memory, identical semantics.

Replace title-attribute tooltips with the focusable tooltip primitive wherever the content is load-bearing (filter reasons, ineligible explanations, event IDs), and surface Plex node dossiers on focus as well as hover so the graph is explorable without a pointer.

Add a single global prefers-reduced-motion rule that collapses all tailwindcss-animate dialog/sheet/pulse animations to instant state changes, reserving the usePrefersReducedMotion hook for canvas/SVG work — motion restraint becomes the default, not a per-component courtesy.
